sentences.zh: 【唐紀七十八】 起上章涒灘，盡重光作噩，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 78] From Shangzhang Tuitan through Chongguang Zuo'e; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 78] From Shangzhang Tuitan through Chongguang Zuo'e—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝中之中光化三年（

translations.literal: Guanghua, year 3, of the middle period of Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, Filial Emperor (
translations.idiomatic: Guanghua, year 3, of the middle reign of Emperor Zhaozong (

sentences.zh: 庚申，公元九零零年）

translations.literal: gengshen, AD 900).
translations.idiomatic: gengshen, AD 900).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，宣州將康儒攻睦州，錢鏐使其從弟銶拒之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Xuanchou general Kang Ru attacked Muzhou; Qian Liu had his younger cousin Qian Qiu resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Xuanchou general Kang Ru attacked Muzhou; Qian Liu sent his younger cousin Qian Qiu to hold him off.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚申，以西川李度使王建兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengshen, Wang Jian, military commissioner of Xichuan, was additionally appointed Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengshen, Wang Jian, military commissioner of Xichuan, was also made Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 壬申，加威武節度使王審知同平章事。

translations.literal: On renshen, Wang Shenzhi, military commissioner of Weiwu, was promoted to Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Weiwu military commissioner Wang Shenzhi was made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以吏部尚書崔胤同平章事，充清海節度使。

translations.literal: On renwu, Cui Yin, Minister of Personnel, was made Grand Councilor and appointed military commissioner of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Minister of Personnel Cui Yin was made Grand Councilor and sent out as military commissioner of Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 李克用大發軍民治晉陽城塹，押牙劉延業諫曰：「大王聲振華、夷，宜揚兵以嚴四境，不宜近治城塹，損威望而啟寇心。」

translations.literal: Li Keyong mobilized soldiers and civilians on a large scale to repair the moat of Jinyang; his yamen guard Liu Yanye remonstrated, saying, "Your Highness's fame resounds through China and the barbarians; you ought to display your forces to awe the four borders—not repair city moats at home, which diminishes prestige and invites enemy designs."
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong drafted soldiers and civilians on a large scale to work on the moat around Jinyang. His guard officer Liu Yanye advised him: "Your Highness's renown reaches across China and beyond; you should parade your armies to overawe the frontiers, not busy yourself with local fortifications, which will lower your prestige and encourage enemies."

sentences.zh: 克用謝之，賞以金帛。

translations.literal: Li Keyong thanked him and rewarded him with gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong thanked him and rewarded him with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，加定難軍節度使李承慶同平章事。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Li Chengqing, military commissioner of the Dingnan Army, was promoted to Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Dingnan military commissioner Li Chengqing was made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣葛從周帥兗、鄆、滑、魏四鎮兵十萬擊劉仁恭，五月，庚寅，拔德州，斬刺史傅公和。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent Ge Congzhou to lead a hundred thousand troops from the four prefectures of Yan, Yun, Hua, and Wei against Liu Rengong; in the fifth month, on gengyin, Dezhou was taken and its prefect Fu Gonghe was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Ge Congzhou at the head of a hundred thousand men from Yan, Yun, Hua, and Wei to attack Liu Rengong. In the fifth month, on gengyin, they captured Dezhou and executed its prefect Fu Gonghe.

sentences.zh: 己亥，圍劉守文於滄州。

translations.literal: On jihai, Liu Shouwen was besieged at Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai they besieged Liu Shouwen in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁恭復遣使卑辭厚禮求救於河東，李克用遣周德威將五千騎出黃澤，攻邢、洺以救之。

translations.literal: Rengong again sent envoys with humble words and rich gifts to seek rescue from Hedong; Li Keyong sent Zhou Dewei with five thousand horsemen out through Huangze to attack Xing and Ming in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong again sent envoys with humble pleas and lavish gifts to Hedong for aid. Li Keyong dispatched Zhou Dewei with five thousand cavalry through Huangze to strike Xing and Ming and relieve him.

sentences.zh: 邕州軍亂，逐節度使李鐬。

translations.literal: The Yongzhou army mutinied and expelled its military commissioner Li Kui.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzhou garrison mutinied and drove out military commissioner Li Kui.

sentences.zh: 鐬借兵鄰道討平之。

translations.literal: Kui borrowed troops from neighboring circuits to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Kui borrowed troops from neighboring circuits to put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸亥，加東川節度使王宗滌同平章事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guihai, Wang Zongdi, military commissioner of Dongchuan, was promoted to Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guihai, Dongchuan military commissioner Wang Zongdi was made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 司空、門下侍郎、同平章事王摶，明達有度量，時稱良相。

translations.literal: Wang Tuan, Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Grand Councilor, was clear-sighted and magnanimous; his contemporaries called him a fine minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tuan, Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Grand Councilor, was clear-minded and broad-minded; people of the time hailed him as an excellent chief minister.

sentences.zh: 上素疾宦官樞密使朱道弼、景務修專橫，崔胤日與上謀去宦官，宦官知之。

translations.literal: The emperor had long resented the eunuch commissioners of military affairs Zhu Daobi and Jing Wuxiu for their domineering ways; Cui Yin daily plotted with the emperor to remove the eunuchs, and the eunuchs learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long hated the eunuch commissioners Zhu Daobi and Jing Wuxiu for their high-handed rule. Cui Yin met with him daily to plot the eunuchs' removal, and the eunuchs found out.

sentences.zh: 由是南、北司益相憎嫉，各結籓鎮為援以相傾奪。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Southern and Northern Bureaus grew ever more mutually hostile, each allying with frontier commands to overthrow the other.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Southern and Northern Bureaus hated each other all the more, each courting military governors as allies in their struggle for power.

sentences.zh: 摶恐其致亂，從容言於上曰：「人君當務明大體，無所偏私。

translations.literal: Tuan feared this would bring disorder and said calmly to the emperor, "A ruler should attend to the great principles and show no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan feared this would spark chaos and said gently to the emperor, "A ruler should keep sight of the larger order and favor no faction.

sentences.zh: 宦官擅權之弊，誰不知之！

translations.literal: Who does not know the harm of eunuchs monopolizing power!
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knows the evil of eunuch monopoly of power!

sentences.zh: 顧其勢未可猝除，宜俟多難漸平，以道消息。

translations.literal: Yet their power cannot be removed in haste; you should wait until many troubles gradually subside and then, by the Way, let the matter fade.
translations.idiomatic: But their strength cannot be uprooted overnight. Wait until the many crises ease, then let the matter dissolve by measured policy.

sentences.zh: 願陛下言勿輕洩以速奸變。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty not to let words leak lightly and hasten treacherous upheaval."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty not to speak carelessly and bring on a treacherous coup."

sentences.zh: 胤聞之，譖摶於上曰：「王摶奸邪，已為道弼輩外應。」

translations.literal: When Yin heard of this, he slandered Tuan to the emperor, saying, "Wang Tuan is treacherous and wicked; he already acts as the outside ally of Daobi and his ilk."
translations.idiomatic: When Yin heard this, he denounced Tuan to the emperor: "Wang Tuan is treacherous; he is already the eunuchs' ally on the outside."

sentences.zh: 上疑之。

translations.literal: The emperor grew suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to doubt him.

sentences.zh: 及胤罷相，意摶排己，愈恨之。

translations.literal: When Yin was later dismissed from the chancellorship, he believed Tuan had engineered his removal and hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin was later removed from the chancellorship, he believed Tuan had pushed him out and hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 及出鎮廣州，遺朱全忠書，具道摶語，令全忠表論之。

translations.literal: When he went out to govern at Guangzhou, he sent Zhu Quanzhong a letter detailing Tuan's words and urging Quanzhong to memorialize against him.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to take up his post at Guangzhou, he wrote Zhu Quanzhong a full account of Tuan's remarks and asked him to submit a memorial attacking Tuan.

sentences.zh: 全忠上言：「胤不可離輔弼之地，摶與敕使相表裡，同危社稷。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong memorialized: "Yin must not be kept from the place of chief assistance; Tuan and the imperial commissioners act inside and outside in concert, jointly endangering the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong memorialized: "Yin must not be kept from court; Tuan and the imperial commissioners work hand in glove and together threaten the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 表連上不已。

translations.literal: Memorials followed one after another without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He sent memorial after memorial without letup.

sentences.zh: 上雖察其情，迫於全忠，不得已，胤至湖南復召還。

translations.literal: Although the emperor saw through the situation, pressed by Quanzhong he had no choice; when Yin reached Hunan he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor saw what was really going on, Quanzhong's pressure left him no choice: Yin was recalled while still on the road in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以胤為司空、門下侍郎、同平章事，摶罷為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Yin was made Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Grand Councilor; Tuan was dismissed and made Vice Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Yin was appointed Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Grand Councilor; Tuan was demoted to Vice Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 以道弼監荊南軍，務修監青州軍。

translations.literal: Daobi was assigned to supervise the Jingnan army; Wuxiu was assigned to supervise the Qingzhou army.
translations.idiomatic: Daobi was sent to oversee the Jingnan army; Wuxiu was sent to oversee the Qingzhou army.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，貶摶溪州刺史；

translations.literal: On wuchen, Tuan was demoted to prefect of Xizhou;
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Tuan was demoted to prefect of Xizhou;

sentences.zh: 己巳，又貶崖州司戶。

translations.literal: on jisi, he was demoted again to registrar of Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: on jisi he was demoted again to registrar of Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 道弼長流歡州，務修長流愛州。

translations.literal: Daobi was exiled far to Huanzhou; Wuxiu was exiled far to Aizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Daobi was banished to distant Huanzhou; Wuxiu was banished to distant Aizhou.

sentences.zh: 是日，皆賜自盡。

translations.literal: That same day, all were granted permission to take their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, all were ordered to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 摶死於藍田驛，道弼、務修死於霸橋驛。

translations.literal: Tuan died at the Lantian post station; Daobi and Wuxiu died at the Baqiao post station.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan died at the Lantian relay; Daobi and Wuxiu died at the Baqiao relay.

sentences.zh: 於是胤專制朝政，勢震中外，宦官皆側目，不勝其憤。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yin monopolized court governance; his power shook the empire inside and out, and the eunuchs glared sideways, unable to contain their rage.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Yin dominated the court; his power awed the realm, and the eunuchs glared at him in helpless fury.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭將幽州兵五萬救滄州，營於乾寧軍。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong led fifty thousand Youzhou troops to relieve Cangzhou and encamped at Qianning Army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong marched fifty thousand Youzhou troops to relieve Cangzhou and camped at Qianning Army.

sentences.zh: 葛從周留張存敬、氏叔琮守滄州寨，自將精兵逆戰於老鴉堤，大破仁恭，斬首三萬級，仁恭走保瓦橋。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou left Zhang Cunjing and Shi Shuzong to hold the Cangzhou camp, himself leading elite troops to meet the enemy at Laoya Embankment; he routed Rengong utterly, taking thirty thousand heads; Rengong fled to hold Waqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou left Zhang Cunjing and Shi Shuzong to guard the Cangzhou camp and led his best troops to meet Rengong at Laoya Embankment. He crushed the relief force, claiming thirty thousand heads, and Rengong fled to Waqiao.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，李克用復遣都指揮使李嗣昭將兵五萬攻邢、洺以救仁恭，敗汴軍於內丘。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Li Keyong again sent the chief commander Li Sizhao with fifty thousand troops to attack Xing and Ming to save Rengong, defeating the Bian army at Neiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Li Keyong again sent chief commander Li Sizhao with fifty thousand men against Xing and Ming to relieve Rengong and defeated the Bian army at Neiqiu.

sentences.zh: 鎔遣使和解幽、汴，會久雨，朱全忠召從周還。

translations.literal: Rong sent envoys to mediate peace between You and Bian; as heavy rains set in, Zhu Quanzhong recalled Congzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sent envoys to broker peace between You and Bian. Prolonged rain fell, and Zhu Quanzhong recalled Congzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以昭義留後孟遷為節度使。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Meng Qian, acting military commissioner of Zhaoyi, was appointed full military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Zhaoyi acting commissioner Meng Qian was confirmed as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以西川節度使王建兼東川、信武軍兩道都指揮制置等使。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Wang Jian, military commissioner of Xichuan, was additionally made overall commander and commissioner for the two circuits of Dongchuan and Xinwu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Xichuan military commissioner Wang Jian was also made overall commander for Dongchuan and Xinwu.

sentences.zh: 八月，李嗣昭又敗汴軍於沙門河，進攻洺州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Li Sizhao again defeated the Bian army at the Shamen River and advanced to besiege Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Li Sizhao again routed the Bian army at the Shamen River and pressed the attack on Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，朱全忠引兵救之，未至，嗣昭拔洺州，擒刺史朱紹宗。

translations.literal: On yichou, Zhu Quanzhong led troops to relieve it, but before he arrived Sizhao took Mingzhou and captured its prefect Zhu Shaozong.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Zhu Quanzhong marched to relieve the city, but before he arrived Sizhao captured Mingzhou and seized its prefect Zhu Shaozong.

sentences.zh: 全忠命葛從周將兵擊嗣昭。

translations.literal: Quanzhong ordered Ge Congzhou to lead troops against Sizhao.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong ordered Ge Congzhou to take the field against Sizhao.

sentences.zh: 宣州將康儒食盡，自清溪遁歸。

translations.literal: The Xuanchou general Kang Ru, his provisions exhausted, fled back from Qingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanchou general Kang Ru, out of food, slipped away from Qingxi and retreated.

sentences.zh: 九月，葛從周自鄴縣渡漳水，營於黃龍鎮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Ge Congzhou crossed the Zhang River from Yexian and encamped at Huanglong Town.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Ge Congzhou crossed the Zhang River from Yexian and camped at Huanglong Town.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠自將中軍三萬涉洺水置營。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong personally led thirty thousand central-army troops across the Ming River and set camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong personally led thirty thousand men of the central army across the Ming River and pitched camp.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭棄城走，從周設伏於青山口，邀擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao abandoned the city and fled; Congzhou laid an ambush at Qingshan Pass, intercepted him, and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao abandoned the city and fled. Congzhou ambushed him at Qingshan Pass, cut him off, and smashed his army.

sentences.zh: 崔胤以太保、門下侍郎、同平章事徐彥若位在己上，惡之。

translations.literal: Cui Yin resented Xu Yanruo, Grand Preceptor, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Grand Councilor, because Yanruo ranked above him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin resented Grand Preceptor, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Grand Councilor Xu Yanruo, who outranked him.

sentences.zh: 彥若亦自求引去。

translations.literal: Yanruo also asked on his own to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Yanruo for his part asked to be relieved of office.

sentences.zh: 時籓鎮皆為強臣所據，惟嗣薛王知柔在廣州，乃求代之。

translations.literal: At the time every frontier command was held by powerful ministers; only the heir Prince of Xue, Zhirou, was at Guangzhou, so he sought to replace him there.
translations.idiomatic: At the time every military governorship was held by a strongman; only the heir Prince of Xue, Zhirou, remained at Guangzhou, so Yanruo asked to take his place.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以彥若同平章事，充清海節度使。

translations.literal: On yisi, Yanruo was made Grand Councilor and appointed military commissioner of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Yanruo was made Grand Councilor and sent out as military commissioner of Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 初，荊南節度成汭以澧、朗本其巡屬，為雷滿所據，屢求割隸荊南。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cheng Jun, military commissioner of Jingnan, held that Li and Lang had originally been under his inspection circuit but were occupied by Lei Man; he repeatedly asked that they be transferred to Jingnan's jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jingnan commissioner Cheng Jun had argued that Li and Lang belonged to his circuit but were held by Lei Man, and he repeatedly petitioned to have them placed under Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不許，汭頗怨望。

translations.literal: The court did not grant this, and Jun was quite resentful.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused, and Jun nursed considerable resentment.

sentences.zh: 及彥若過荊南，汭置酒，從容以為言。

translations.literal: When Yanruo passed through Jingnan, Jun set out wine and spoke of the matter at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanruo passed through Jingnan, Jun entertained him with wine and raised the matter in easy conversation.

sentences.zh: 彥若曰：「令公位尊方面，自比桓、文，雷滿小盜不能取，乃怨朝廷乎？」

translations.literal: Yanruo said, "Your Lordship holds a lofty post on the frontier and compares yourself to Duke Huan and Duke Wen—yet you cannot take a petty bandit like Lei Man and instead resent the court?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanruo said, "You hold a great frontier command and liken yourself to Duke Huan and Duke Wen—yet you cannot deal with a petty bandit like Lei Man and blame the court instead?"

sentences.zh: 汭甚慚。

translations.literal: Jun was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 丙午，中書侍郎兼吏部尚書、同平章事崔遠罷守本官，以刑部尚書裴贄為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Cui Yuan, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Personnel and Grand Councilor, was dismissed to his original office; Pei Zan, Minister of Justice, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Grand Councilor Cui Yuan, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Personnel, was removed to his former post; Minister of Justice Pei Zan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 贄，坦之弟子也。

translations.literal: Zan was a nephew-disciple of Pei Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was a nephew of Pei Tan.

sentences.zh: 升桂管為靜江軍，以經略使劉士政為節度使。

translations.literal: Guiguan was promoted to the Jingjiang Army; Liu Shizheng, frontier commissioner, was made its military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Guiguan was elevated to the Jingjiang Army circuit, and frontier commissioner Liu Shizheng was appointed its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠以王鎔與李克用交通，移兵伐之，下臨城，逾滹沱，攻鎮州南門，焚其關城。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong, because Wang Rong was in communication with Li Keyong, shifted troops to attack him, took Lincheng, crossed the Hutuo, assaulted the south gate of Zhenzhou, and burned its barrier city.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wang Rong was in contact with Li Keyong, Zhu Quanzhong marched against him, captured Lincheng, crossed the Hutuo, attacked the south gate of Zhenzhou, and burned its outer fortifications.

sentences.zh: 全忠自至元氏，鎔懼，遣判官周式詣全忠請和。

translations.literal: Quanzhong himself advanced to Yuanshi; Rong was afraid and sent his aide Zhou Shi to Quanzhong to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong advanced in person to Yuanshi. Rong was terrified and sent his secretary Zhou Shi to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 全忠盛怒，謂式曰：「僕屢以書諭王公，竟不之聽！

translations.literal: Quanzhong was furious and said to Shi, "I have repeatedly written to instruct Lord Wang, yet he would not heed!
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was furious and told Shi, "I have written again and again to Lord Wang, and he would not listen!

sentences.zh: 今兵已至此。

translations.literal: Now my army has come this far.
translations.idiomatic: Now my army is here.

sentences.zh: 期於無捨！」

translations.literal: I expect no sparing!"
translations.idiomatic: I intend to show no mercy!"

sentences.zh: 式曰：「鎮州密邇太原，困於侵暴，四鄰各自保，莫相救恤，王公與之連和，乃為百姓故也。

translations.literal: Shi said, "Zhenzhou lies close to Taiyuan and is harried by invasion and violence; the four neighboring circuits each look to their own defense and offer no mutual aid. Lord Wang allied with them only for the people's sake.
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "Zhenzhou borders Taiyuan and suffers constant raids. The neighboring circuits each look to their own safety and offer no help. Lord Wang allied with Hedong only to protect his people.

sentences.zh: 今明公果能為人除害，則天下誰不聽命，豈惟鎮州！

translations.literal: If Your Lordship can truly remove harm for others, who under Heaven would not obey—how much less Zhenzhou alone!
translations.idiomatic: If you truly rid the realm of this scourge, who under Heaven would not follow you—not Zhenzhou alone!

sentences.zh: 明公為唐桓、文，當崇禮義以成霸業。

translations.literal: Your Lordship would be the Huan and Wen of Tang; you should exalt ritual and righteousness to complete a hegemonic enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: You aspire to be the Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Tang; you should uphold ritual and righteousness to build a true hegemony.

sentences.zh: 若但窮威武，則鎮州雖小，城堅食足，明公雖有十萬之眾，未易攻也！

translations.literal: If you rely only on brute force, then though Zhenzhou is small, its walls are strong and its provisions ample; though Your Lordship has a host of a hundred thousand, it will not be easy to take!
translations.idiomatic: If you rely on force alone, Zhenzhou is small but its walls are strong and its stores full. Even with a hundred thousand men, you will not take it easily!

sentences.zh: 況王氏秉旄五代，時推忠孝，人人欲為之死，庸可冀乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover the Wang house has borne the standard for five generations; the age praises their loyalty and filial piety—every man wishes to die for them. How can you hope for success!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Wangs have held command for five generations and are famed for loyalty and filial piety. Every man is ready to die for them. What success can you expect?"

sentences.zh: 全忠笑攬式袂，延之帳中，曰：「與公戲耳！」

translations.literal: Quanzhong laughed, took Shi's sleeve, and led him into the tent, saying, "I was only jesting with you!"
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong laughed, took Shi's sleeve, and led him into his tent. "I was only teasing you!"

sentences.zh: 乃遣客將開封劉捍入見鎔，鎔以其子節度副使昭祚及大將子弟為質，以文繒二十萬犒軍。

translations.literal: He then sent his guest officer Liu Han of Kaifeng to see Rong; Rong gave his son, deputy military commissioner Zhaozuo, and the sons of his great generals as hostages, and presented two hundred thousand bolts of patterned silk to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his liaison officer Liu Han of Kaifeng to see Rong. Rong gave his son, deputy commissioner Zhaozuo, and the sons of his chief generals as hostages and sent two hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army.

sentences.zh: 全忠引還，以女妻昭祚。

translations.literal: Quanzhong withdrew and gave his daughter in marriage to Zhaozuo.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong withdrew and gave his daughter in marriage to Zhaozuo.

sentences.zh: 成德判官張澤言於王鎔曰：「河東，勍敵也，今雖有朱氏之援，譬如火發於家，安能俟遠水乎！

translations.literal: Zhang Ze, aide of Chengde, said to Wang Rong, "Hedong is a formidable foe; though you now have the Zhu clan's aid, it is like fire breaking out in the house—how can you wait for distant water!
translations.idiomatic: Chengde aide Zhang Ze told Wang Rong, "Hedong is a formidable enemy. Zhu's help is like trying to put out a house fire with water from far away.

sentences.zh: 彼幽、滄易定。

translations.literal: You and Cang are easy to settle.
translations.idiomatic: You and Cang can be taken easily.

sentences.zh: 猶附河東，不若說朱公乘勝兼服之，使河北諸鎮合而為一，則可以制河東矣。」

translations.literal: Yet you still cling to Hedong; better to urge Lord Zhu, while victory is fresh, to subdue them as well, unite the Hebei commands into one, and then you can control Hedong."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you still lean on Hedong. Better urge Lord Zhu, while he is winning, to conquer them too, unite the Hebei commands, and then you can master Hedong."

sentences.zh: 鎔復遣周式往說全忠。

translations.literal: Rong again sent Zhou Shi to persuade Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Rong again sent Zhou Shi to persuade Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 全忠喜，遣張存敬會魏博兵擊劉仁恭，甲寅，拔瀛州；

translations.literal: Quanzhong was pleased and sent Zhang Cunjing to join Weibo troops in attacking Liu Rengong; on jiayin, Yingzhou was taken;
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was delighted and sent Zhang Cunjing to join Weibo forces against Liu Rengong. On jiayin they took Yingzhou;

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙辰，拔景州，執刺史劉仁霸；

translations.literal: in winter, the tenth month, on bingchen, Jingzhou was taken and its prefect Liu Renba was captured;
translations.idiomatic: in winter, the tenth month, on bingchen they took Jingzhou and seized its prefect Liu Renba;

sentences.zh: 辛酉，拔莫州。

translations.literal: on xinyou, Mozhou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: on xinyou they took Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 靜江節度使劉士政聞馬殷悉平嶺北，大懼，遣副使陳可璠屯全義嶺以備之。

translations.literal: Liu Shizheng, military commissioner of Jingjiang, heard that Ma Yin had entirely pacified north of the ranges and was greatly afraid; he sent his deputy Chen Kelin to garrison Quanyi Ridge in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjiang commissioner Liu Shizheng, hearing that Ma Yin had pacified all the country north of the ranges, was terrified and sent his deputy Chen Kelin to hold Quanyi Ridge against him.

sentences.zh: 殷遣使修好於士政，可璠拒之。

translations.literal: Yin sent envoys to establish good relations with Shizheng; Kelin refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent envoys to offer friendship; Kelin turned them away.

sentences.zh: 殷遣其將秦彥暉、李瓊等將兵七千擊士政。

translations.literal: Yin sent his generals Qin Yanhui, Li Qiong, and others with seven thousand troops to attack Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent his generals Qin Yanhui and Li Qiong with seven thousand men against Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 湖南軍至全義，士政又遣指揮使王建武屯秦城。

translations.literal: When the Hunan army reached Quanyi, Shizheng again sent the commander Wang Jianwu to garrison Qincheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hunan army reached Quanyi, Shizheng sent commander Wang Jianwu to hold Qincheng.

sentences.zh: 可璠掠縣民耕牛以犒軍，縣民怨之，請為湖南鄉異，曰：「此西南有小徑，距秦城才五十里，僅通單騎。」

translations.literal: Kelin seized the county people's draft oxen to reward the army; the county people resented this and asked to serve as Hunan guides, saying, "To the southwest there is a small path only fifty li from Qincheng, passable for single horsemen alone."
translations.idiomatic: Kelin seized local farmers' oxen to reward his troops. The locals, resenting this, offered to guide the Hunan army and said, "A small path southwest of here reaches Qincheng in only fifty li—wide enough for a single horse."

sentences.zh: 彥暉遣李瓊將騎六十、步兵三百襲秦城，中宵，逾垣而入，擒王建武，比明，復還，絲斥之以練，造可璠壁下示之，可璠猶未之信。

translations.literal: Yanhui sent Li Qiong with sixty horsemen and three hundred foot soldiers to raid Qincheng; at midnight they scaled the wall and entered, capturing Wang Jianwu; by dawn they returned, bound him with silk cords, and displayed him below Kelin's ramparts—yet Kelin still did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui sent Li Qiong with sixty cavalry and three hundred infantry to strike Qincheng. At midnight they scaled the walls, seized Wang Jianwu, and by dawn were back. They bound him with silk cords and displayed him below Kelin's walls, but Kelin still would not believe it.

sentences.zh: 斬其首，投壁中，桂人震恐。

translations.literal: They beheaded him and cast the head over the wall; the people of Gui were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: They beheaded him and threw the head over the wall. The Gui troops were terrified.

sentences.zh: 瓊因勒兵擊之，擒可璠，降其將士二千，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Qiong then led troops to attack him, captured Kelin, and received the surrender of two thousand officers and soldiers—all of whom were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong then attacked in force, captured Kelin, and accepted the surrender of two thousand officers and men—all of whom were executed.

sentences.zh: 引兵趣桂州，自秦城以南二十餘壁皆望風奔潰，遂圍桂州。

translations.literal: He led his army toward Guizhou; more than twenty fortified posts south of Qincheng collapsed at the mere sight of his banners, and he then besieged Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Guizhou. More than twenty fortified posts south of Qincheng fled at his approach, and he laid siege to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 數日，士政出降，桂、宜、巖、柳、象五州皆降於湖南。

translations.literal: Within several days Shizheng came out and surrendered; the five prefectures of Gui, Yi, Yan, Liu, and Xiang all submitted to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Shizheng surrendered. The five prefectures of Gui, Yi, Yan, Liu, and Xiang all submitted to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 馬殷以李瓊為桂州刺史，未幾，表為靜江節度使。

translations.literal: Ma Yin appointed Li Qiong prefect of Guizhou; before long he memorialized to make him military commissioner of Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin made Li Qiong prefect of Guizhou and soon memorialized to appoint him military commissioner of Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 張存敬攻劉仁恭，下二十城，將自瓦橋趣幽州，道濘不能進，乃引兵西攻易定，辛巳，拔祁州，殺刺史楊約。

translations.literal: Zhang Cunjing attacked Liu Rengong, took twenty cities, and was about to advance from Waqiao toward Youzhou, but the roads were mired and he could not proceed; he therefore led his army west to attack Yiding; on xinsi, Qizhou was taken and its prefect Yang Yue was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cunjing attacked Liu Rengong and captured twenty cities. He planned to march from Waqiao on Youzhou, but the roads were too muddy to advance, so he turned west against Yiding. On xinsi he took Qizhou and killed its prefect Yang Yue.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以保義留後朱友謙為節度使。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Zhu Youqian, acting military commissioner of Baoyi, was appointed full military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Baoyi acting commissioner Zhu Youqian was confirmed as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 張存敬攻定州，義武節度使王郜遣後院都知兵馬使王處直將兵數萬拒之。

translations.literal: Zhang Cunjing attacked Dingzhou; Wang Gao, military commissioner of Yiwu, sent Wang Chuzhi, commander of the rear courtyard, with tens of thousands of troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cunjing attacked Dingzhou. Yiwu commissioner Wang Gao sent rear-court commander Wang Chuzhi with tens of thousands of men to resist him.

sentences.zh: 處直請依城為柵，俟其師老而擊之。

translations.literal: Chuzhi asked to build palisades by the city and wait until the enemy army grew weary before striking.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi proposed building palisades by the city and waiting until the enemy grew tired before attacking.

sentences.zh: 孔目官梁汶曰：「昔幽、鎮兵三十萬攻我，於時我軍不滿五千，一戰敗之。

translations.literal: The clerical officer Liang Wen said, "Formerly three hundred thousand You and Zhen troops attacked us when our army numbered fewer than five thousand, yet in one battle we defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Liang Wen said, "When three hundred thousand You and Zhen troops attacked us, we had fewer than five thousand men—and we routed them in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 今存敬兵不過三萬，我軍十倍於昔，奈何示怯，欲依城自固乎！」

translations.literal: Now Cunjing's troops are no more than thirty thousand; our army is ten times what it was then—why show weakness and wish to rely on the city for self-defense!
translations.idiomatic: Cunjing has barely thirty thousand men, while we outnumber our old force tenfold—why act timid and hide behind the walls?

sentences.zh: 郜乃遣處直逆戰於沙河，易定兵大敗，死者過半，餘眾擁處直奔還。

translations.literal: Gao then sent Chuzhi to meet the enemy in battle at the Sha River; the Yiding troops were utterly defeated, more than half were killed, and the remnant crowd escorted Chuzhi straight back in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent Chuzhi to fight at the Sha River. The Yiding army was crushed; over half the men died, and the survivors fled, crowding Chuzhi back to safety.

sentences.zh: 甲申，王郜棄城奔晉陽，軍中推處直為留後。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Wang Gao abandoned the city and fled to Jinyang; the army within pushed Chuzhi to serve as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Wang Gao abandoned the city and fled to Jinyang. The troops made Chuzhi acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 存敬進圍定州，丙申，朱全忠至城下，處直登城呼曰：「本道事朝廷盡忠，於公未嘗相犯，何為見攻？」

translations.literal: Cunjing pressed on to besiege Dingzhou; on bingshen, Zhu Quanzhong came beneath the city walls; Chuzhi ascended the wall and called out: "This circuit has served the court with full loyalty; toward you, sir, we have never offered offense—why are we being attacked?
translations.idiomatic: Cunjing continued the siege of Dingzhou. On bingshen Zhu Quanzhong arrived at the walls. Chuzhi climbed up and shouted: "Our circuit has always been loyal to the court and never wronged you—why attack us?

sentences.zh: 全忠曰：「何故附河東？」

translations.literal: Quanzhong said: "Why attach yourself to Hedong?"
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong replied: "Why have you sided with Hedong?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「吾兄與晉王同時立勳，封疆密邇，且婚姻也，修好往來，乃常理耳，請從茲改圖。」

translations.literal: He answered: "My elder brother and the Prince of Jin won merit at the same time; our border territories lie close together, and moreover we are linked by marriage—maintaining friendly exchanges is only normal; please let us change course from this point."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "My brother and the Prince of Jin won glory together. Our domains border each other and we are joined by marriage—friendly ties are only natural. Please let us mend matters from here."

sentences.zh: 全忠許之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong agreed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong accepted.

sentences.zh: 乃歸罪於梁汶而族之，以謝全忠，以繒帛十萬犒師。

translations.literal: He then placed the blame on Liang Wen and exterminated his clan, to apologize to Quanzhong, and gave one hundred thousand worth of silks and fabrics to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed Liang Wen, executed his entire clan as an apology to Quanzhong, and presented one hundred thousand in silk goods to reward the army.

sentences.zh: 全忠乃還，仍為處直表求節鉞。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then returned, and still memorialized on Chuzhi's behalf requesting the seal and axe of command.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong withdrew, but memorialized the court to grant Chuzhi full military commission.

sentences.zh: 處直，處存之母弟也。

translations.literal: Chuzhi was Chucun's younger brother by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi was Chucun's younger maternal half-brother.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭遣其子守光將兵救定州，軍於易水之上。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong sent his son Shouguang leading troops to rescue Dingzhou, encamping above the Yishui River.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong sent his son Shouguang with an army to relieve Dingzhou, camped on the north bank of the Yishui.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣張存敬襲之，殺六萬餘人。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Zhang Cunjing to strike them, killing more than sixty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Zhang Cunjing to attack them and slew more than sixty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 由是河北諸鎮皆服於全忠。

translations.literal: From this, all the circuits of Hebei submitted to Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: After this, every circuit in Hebei acknowledged Quanzhong's authority.

sentences.zh: 先是王郜告急於河東，李克用遣李嗣昭將步騎三萬下太行，攻懷州，拔之，進攻河陽。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Gao had reported emergency to Hedong; Li Keyong sent Li Sizhao leading thirty thousand infantry and cavalry down the Taihang Mountains, attacked Huaizhou, took it, and advanced to attack Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Gao had appealed to Hedong for help. Li Keyong sent Li Sizhao with thirty thousand foot and horse down the Taihang, captured Huaizhou, and pressed on against Heyang.

sentences.zh: 河陽留後侯言不意其至，狼狽失據，嗣昭壞其羊馬城。

translations.literal: Hou Yan, acting commissioner of Heyang, did not expect their arrival; flustered he lost his footing, and Sizhao destroyed his sheep-and-horse wall.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang commissioner Hou Yan was caught completely off guard. Sizhao tore down his outer palisade.

sentences.zh: 會佑國軍將閻寶引兵救之，力戰於壕外，河東兵乃退。

translations.literal: Just then Yan Bao, general of the Youguo Army, led troops to rescue him; they fought fiercely outside the moat, and the Hedong troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bao of the Youguo Army arrived with reinforcements and fought fiercely beyond the moat until the Hedong forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 寶，鄆州人也。

translations.literal: Bao was a man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bao was from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，崔胤與上密謀盡誅宦官，及宋道弼、景務修死，宦官益懼。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Yin had secretly plotted with the emperor to execute all the eunuchs entirely; when Song Daobu and Jing Wuxiu died, the eunuchs grew ever more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Yin had secretly plotted with the emperor to wipe out the eunuchs. After Song Daobu and Jing Wuxiu were killed, the eunuchs grew more afraid.

sentences.zh: 上自華州還，忽忽不樂，多縱酒，喜怒不常，左右尤自危。

translations.literal: After the emperor returned from Huazhou, he was restless and unhappy, indulged much in wine, and his joy and anger were irregular—those around him felt especially imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from Huazhou the emperor was restless and drank heavily, his mood swinging wildly. Those close to him felt especially endangered.

sentences.zh: 於是左軍中尉劉季述、右宮中尉王仲先、樞密使王彥范、薛齊偓等陰相與謀曰：「主上輕佻多變詐，難奉事；

translations.literal: Thereupon the Left Army Commander Liu Jishu, Right Palace Commander Wang Zhongxian, and the Palace Secretaries Wang Yanfan and Xue Qiwo secretly plotted together, saying: "The sovereign is frivolous, much given to change and trickery, and hard to serve;
translations.idiomatic: Then Left Army Commander Liu Jishu, Right Palace Commander Wang Zhongxian, and Palace Secretaries Wang Yanfan and Xue Qiwo secretly conspired: "The emperor is fickle and deceptive—impossible to serve faithfully;

sentences.zh: 專聽任南司，吾輩終罹其禍。

translations.literal: he listens exclusively to and relies upon the southern offices—we in the end will suffer disaster from it.
translations.idiomatic: he listens only to the civil officials—we will be ruined in the end.

sentences.zh: 不若奉太子立之，尊主上為太上皇，引岐、華兵為援，控制諸籓，誰能害我哉！」

translations.literal: Better to install the crown prince and make him sovereign, honor the sovereign as retired emperor, bring Qi and Hua troops as aid, and control the various frontier commands—who could harm us then!"
translations.idiomatic: Better to put the crown prince on the throne, declare the emperor retired, bring in troops from Qi and Hua, and control the frontier lords—who could touch us then!"

sentences.zh: 十一月，上獵苑中，因置酒，夜，醉歸，手殺黃門、侍女數人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the emperor hunted in the imperial park, then set out wine; at night, drunk he returned and personally killed several yellow-gate attendants and palace maids.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor hunted in the park and held a feast. That night he returned drunk and personally killed several eunuchs and palace girls.

sentences.zh: 明旦，日加辰巳，宮門不開。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, when the day had reached the chen and si hours, the palace gates did not open.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the sun passed the chen and si hours, yet the palace gates remained shut.

sentences.zh: 季述詣中書白崔胤曰：「宮中必有變，我內臣也，得以便宜從事，請入視之。」

translations.literal: Jishu went to the Secretariat and informed Cui Yin: "There must be disorder in the palace; I am an inner official and may act as expedient requires—please let me enter to investigate."
translations.idiomatic: Jishu went to the Secretariat and told Cui Yin: "Something has gone wrong in the palace. As an inner official I may act on my own authority—please let me go in and see."

sentences.zh: 乃帥禁兵千人破門而入，訪問，具得其狀。

translations.literal: He then led a thousand palace guards, broke the gate and entered, inquired, and fully learned the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: He then led a thousand imperial guards, broke down the gates, and learned the full story through inquiry.

sentences.zh: 出，謂胤曰：「主上所為如是，豈可理天下！

translations.literal: Coming out, he said to Yin: "The sovereign's conduct is like this—how can he govern the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Emerging, he told Yin: "With the emperor behaving like this, how can he rule the realm!

sentences.zh: 廢昏立明，自古有之，為社稷大計，非不順也。」

translations.literal: Removing the dim and installing the bright has existed since antiquity; for the great plan of the altars of state, it is not unfitting.
translations.idiomatic: Deposing a bad ruler and enthroning a good one is an ancient precedent—it serves the nation and is perfectly legitimate.

sentences.zh: 胤畏死，不敢違。

translations.literal: Yin feared death and did not dare disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, fearing for his life, dared not refuse.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，季述召百官，陳兵殿庭，作胤等連名狀，請太子監國，以示之，使署名。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Jishu summoned the hundred officials, arrayed troops in the palace courtyard, drew up a joint petition in Yin and others' names requesting the crown prince to oversee the state, showed it to them, and made them sign.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Jishu summoned the officials, lined troops in the palace courtyard, presented a joint memorial in Yin's name asking the crown prince to govern, and forced them to sign.

sentences.zh: 胤及百官不得已皆署之。

translations.literal: Yin and the hundred officials, with no alternative, all signed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and the rest of the officials signed under duress.

sentences.zh: 上在乞巧樓，季述、仲先伏將士千人於門外，與宣武進奏官程巖等十餘人入請對。

translations.literal: The emperor was at the Qiqiao Tower; Jishu and Zhongxian concealed a thousand officers and soldiers outside the gate, and with more than ten men including the Xuanwu memorial courier Cheng Yan entered requesting audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at the Qiqiao Tower. Jishu and Zhongxian hid a thousand soldiers outside and entered with Cheng Yan and more than ten Xuanwu couriers to request an audience.

sentences.zh: 季述、仲先甫登殿，將士大呼，突入宣化門，至思政殿前，逢宮人，輒殺之。

translations.literal: Jishu and Zhongxian had just ascended the hall when the officers and soldiers shouted loudly, burst through the Xuanhua Gate, reached before the Sizheng Hall, and whenever they met palace women, immediately killed them.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Jishu and Zhongxian stepped onto the dais, the troops shouted and stormed through the Xuanhua Gate to the Sizheng Hall, killing every palace woman they met.

sentences.zh: 上見兵入，驚墮床下，起，將走，季述、仲先掖之令坐。

translations.literal: The emperor saw troops enter, startled fell from the bed, rose and was about to flee; Jishu and Zhongxian supported him and made him sit.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor saw armed men rush in, he fell from the bed in fright and tried to run; Jishu and Zhongxian seized him and forced him to sit.

sentences.zh: 宮人走白皇后，-{后}-趨至，拜請曰：「軍容勿驚宅家，有事取軍容商量。」

translations.literal: Palace women ran to inform the empress; the empress hurried to the spot, bowed and pleaded: "Army Commander, do not startle His Majesty; if there is business, take it up with Army Commander for discussion."
translations.idiomatic: Palace women ran to tell the empress. The empress rushed over, bowed, and pleaded: "Army Commander, please do not alarm His Majesty. Whatever the matter, discuss it with you."

sentences.zh: 季述等乃出百官狀白上，曰：「陛下厭倦大寶，中外群情，願太子監國，請陛下保頤東宮。」

translations.literal: Jishu and the others then produced the officials' petition and reported to the emperor, saying: "Your Majesty has grown weary of the great throne; sentiment within and without wishes the crown prince to oversee the state—please Your Majesty nurture your health in the Eastern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Jishu and his followers then showed the emperor the officials' memorial and said: "Your Majesty is weary of reigning. Court and country alike want the crown prince to govern. Please retire to the Eastern Palace for your health."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「昨與卿曹樂飲，不覺太過，何至於是！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yesterday I drank merrily with you all and did not notice going too far—how did it come to this!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Last night I was drinking with you and got carried away—how did it come to this!

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此非臣等所為，皆南司眾情，不可遏也。

translations.literal: They answered: "This is not what we ministers did—it is the general sentiment of the southern offices and cannot be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: They replied: "This is not our doing. It is the unanimous will of the civil officials and cannot be stopped.

sentences.zh: 願陛下且之東宮，待事小定，復迎歸大內耳。」

translations.literal: We wish Your Majesty for now to go to the Eastern Palace; wait until matters are slightly settled, then we will welcome you back to the inner palace—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Please go to the Eastern Palace for now. When things settle, we will bring you back to the palace."

sentences.zh: -{后}-曰：「宅家趣依軍容語！」

translations.literal: The empress said: "His Majesty, quickly follow Army Commander's words!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "Your Majesty, do as the Army Commander says—now!"

sentences.zh: 即取傳國寶以授季述，宦官扶上與-{后}-同輦，嬪御侍從者才十餘人，適少陽院。

translations.literal: Immediately she took the imperial seal of transmission and handed it to Jishu; eunuchs supported the emperor and rode in the same carriage with the empress; concubines and attendants numbered only a little more than ten—they went to the Shaoyang Courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: She handed the imperial seal to Jishu. Eunuchs helped the emperor and the empress into a carriage with barely a dozen attendants and took them to the Shaoyang Courtyard.

sentences.zh: 季述以銀檛畫地數上曰：「某時某事，汝不從我言，其罪一也。」

translations.literal: Jishu used a silver mace to strike the ground counting off to the emperor: "At such a time such a matter—you did not obey my words: that is one offense."
translations.idiomatic: Jishu rapped the ground with a silver mace and listed the emperor's offenses: "On such and such an occasion you defied me—that is one crime."

sentences.zh: 如此數十不止。

translations.literal: Like this he counted dozens and did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: He went on listing dozens of such charges without stopping.

sentences.zh: 乃手鎖其門，熔鐵錮之，遣左軍副使李師虔將兵圍之，上動靜輒白季述，穴牆以通飲食，凡兵器針刀皆不得入，上求錢帛俱不得，求紙筆亦不與。

translations.literal: He then personally locked the door and sealed it with molten iron; dispatched the Left Army deputy envoy Li Shiqian leading troops to surround it; the emperor's every movement was reported to Jishu; a hole was bored in the wall to pass food and drink; all weapons, needles and blades were forbidden entry; the emperor asked for cash and silks but obtained none, asked for paper and brush and was not given them either.
translations.idiomatic: He locked the door and sealed it with molten iron, posted Li Shiqian and troops to guard the place, and reported the emperor's every move to Jishu. Food came through a hole in the wall; no weapons, needles, or knives were allowed in. The emperor could get neither money nor silk, nor even paper and ink.

sentences.zh: 時大寒，嬪御公主無衣衾，號哭聞於外。

translations.literal: At the time the cold was extreme; concubines and imperial princesses had no clothing or coverlets, and their wailing was heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: It was bitterly cold. The concubines and princesses lacked quilts, and their cries could be heard outside.

sentences.zh: 季述等矯詔令太子監國，迎太子入宮。

translations.literal: Jishu and the others forged an edict ordering the crown prince to oversee the state and welcomed the crown prince into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu forged an edict putting the crown prince in charge of government and brought him into the palace.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，矯詔令太子嗣位，更名縝。

translations.literal: On xinmao, a forged edict ordered the crown prince to succeed to the throne; his name was changed to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao a forged edict enthroned the crown prince and renamed him Chen.

sentences.zh: 以上為太上皇，皇后為太上皇后。

translations.literal: The emperor was made retired emperor; the empress was made retired empress.
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor was styled Retired Emperor; the empress became Retired Empress.

sentences.zh: 甲午，太子即皇帝位，更名少陽院曰問安宮。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the crown prince assumed the emperor's throne and renamed the Shaoyang Courtyard the Wen'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the crown prince took the throne and renamed the Shaoyang Courtyard the Palace of Inquiring After His Health.

sentences.zh: 季述加百官爵秩，與將士皆受優賞，欲以求媚於眾。

translations.literal: Jishu increased the ranks and titles of the hundred officials; officers and soldiers alike received generous rewards, wishing thereby to curry favor with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu promoted officials and richly rewarded the troops, trying to buy popularity.

sentences.zh: 殺睦王倚，凡宮人、左右、方士、僧、道為上所寵信者，皆榜殺之。

translations.literal: He killed Prince Mu Yi; all palace women, attendants, alchemical masters, monks, and Daoists whom the emperor had favored and trusted were beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Prince Mu Yi and had beaten to death every palace woman, attendant, alchemist, monk, and Daoist the emperor had favored.

sentences.zh: 每夜殺人，晝以十車載屍出，一車或止一兩屍，欲以立威。

translations.literal: Each night he killed people; by day ten carts carried corpses out—one cart might hold only one or two corpses—intending to establish authority through terror.
translations.idiomatic: Every night brought killings; by day ten carts hauled corpses out, sometimes only one or two to a cart, all to terrify the court.

sentences.zh: 將殺司天監胡秀林，秀林曰：「軍容幽囚君父，更欲多殺無辜乎！」

translations.literal: About to kill the Director of the Astronomy Bureau Hu Xiulin, Xiulin said: "Army Commander, you have imprisoned the emperor and his father—do you further wish to kill many innocents!"
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to execute Hu Xiulin, director of the Astronomy Bureau, Xiulin said: "Army Commander, you have already imprisoned the sovereign—will you now slaughter the innocent as well?"

sentences.zh: 季述憚其言正而止。

translations.literal: Jishu, fearing his words were upright, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu, struck by the rebuke, held back.

sentences.zh: 季述等欲殺崔胤，而憚朱全忠，但解其度支監督鐵轉運使而已。

translations.literal: Jishu and the others wished to kill Cui Yin but feared Zhu Quanzhong; they only removed him from his posts as director of the Department of Public Works supervising iron and transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu wanted to kill Cui Yin but feared Zhu Quanzhong, so he merely stripped Yin of his fiscal and iron-transport posts.

sentences.zh: 崔胤密緻書全忠，使興兵圖返正。

translations.literal: Cui Yin secretly sent a carefully composed letter to Quanzhong, urging him to raise troops and plan restoration of legitimate rule.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin secretly wrote Quanzhong, urging him to raise an army and restore the rightful ruler.

sentences.zh: 左僕射致仕張濬在長水，見張全義於洛陽，勸之匡復，又與諸籓鎮書勸之。

translations.literal: Retired Left Vice Director Zhang Jun was at Changshui; he saw Zhang Quanyi at Luoyang and urged him to restore the dynasty; he also wrote letters to the various frontier commands urging them.
translations.idiomatic: Retired Left Vice Director Zhang Jun, staying at Changshui, met Zhang Quanyi in Luoyang and urged restoration. He also wrote to the frontier commands urging the same.

sentences.zh: 進士無棣李愚客遊華州，上韓建書，略曰：「僕每讀書，見君臣父子之際，有傷教害義者，恨不得肆之市朝。

translations.literal: Presented Scholar Li Yu of Wudi, traveling as a guest, was in Huazhou; he submitted a letter to Han Jian, in summary saying: "Whenever I read books and see at the juncture of ruler and minister, father and son, conduct that wounds teaching and harms righteousness, I cannot but wish to expose it in the marketplace and court.
translations.idiomatic: Presented Scholar Li Yu of Wudi, guesting in Huazhou, wrote Han Jian a letter that opened: "In my reading, whenever I see conduct between ruler and subject or father and son that violates decency, I wish the offender could be exposed in the public square.

sentences.zh: 明公居近關重鎮，君父幽辱月餘，坐視凶逆而忘勤王之舉，僕所未諭也。

translations.literal: Your Excellency occupies a key post near the Pass; the emperor and father has endured disgrace in confinement for more than a month—you sit and watch the vicious rebels and forget the action of rushing to aid the sovereign: this I cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: You hold a critical post near the capital. The emperor has languished in shame for over a month, yet you watch the rebels and forget your duty to rescue him—that I cannot understand.

sentences.zh: 僕竊計中朝輔弼，雖有志而無權；

translations.literal: I privately reckon that among the assisting ministers of the central court, though some have aspiration they have no power;
translations.idiomatic: I reckon that at court the ministers may have will but no power;

sentences.zh: 外鎮諸侯，雖有權而無志。

translations.literal: the frontier lords of the outer commands, though having power have no aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: while the frontier lords have power but no will to act.

sentences.zh: 惟明公忠義，社稷是依。

translations.literal: Only Your Excellency's loyalty and righteousness—the altars of soil and grain rely upon you.
translations.idiomatic: You alone combine loyalty and righteousness—the realm depends on you.

sentences.zh: 往年車輅播遷，號泣奉迎，累歲供饋，再復廟、朝，義感人心，至今歌詠。

translations.literal: In former years when the imperial carriage wandered in exile, you received it with weeping welcome; for years you supplied provisions; you twice restored the ancestral temple and court audiences—righteousness moved men's hearts, and to this day people sing of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was driven into exile you wept as you welcomed it back, fed the court for years, and restored the temples and audiences—deeds men still praise in song.

sentences.zh: 此時事勢，尤異前日，明公地處要衝，位兼將相。

translations.literal: The situation at this time is especially different from before; Your Excellency's territory sits at a vital crossing, your position combines general and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Today's crisis is graver still, and you stand at the crossroads as both general and minister.

sentences.zh: 自宮闈變故，已涉旬時，若不號令率先以圖反正，遲疑未決，一朝山東侯伯唱義連衡，彭行而西，明公求欲自安，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Since the inner palace upheaval, more than ten days have passed; if you do not issue orders and take the lead to plan restoration, hesitating undecided—once the lords of the east raise righteous banners and ally together, advancing west like a tidal bore, if Your Excellency seeks to keep yourself safe, how could that be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: The palace coup is already ten days old. If you do not lead a restoration now, and eastern lords rise in alliance and march west, how will you keep yourself safe?

sentences.zh: 此必然之勢也。

translations.literal: This is the inevitable tendency.
translations.idiomatic: That outcome is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 不如馳檄四方，諭以逆順，軍聲一振，則元凶破膽，旬浹之間，二豎之首傳於天下，計無便於此者。」

translations.literal: Better to dispatch proclamations in all directions, instructing them in loyalty and rebellion; once military renown shakes once, then the chief culprit will break his gall; within ten days the heads of the two swine will be transmitted throughout the realm—no plan is more convenient than this."
translations.idiomatic: Better to proclaim the righteous cause across the land. One show of force will terrify the culprits; within ten days the heads of those two villains could be displayed to the empire—no better plan exists."

sentences.zh: 建雖不能用，厚待之，愚堅辭而去。

translations.literal: Jian although unable to act on it, treated him generously; Yu firmly declined and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian could not act on the advice but treated Yu well; Yu politely refused to stay and left.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠在定州行營，聞亂，丁未，南還。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was at the Dingzhou field headquarters; hearing of the disorder, on dingwei he returned south.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong was campaigning at Dingzhou. When he heard of the coup, he marched south on dingwei.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊辰，至大梁。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuchen, he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuchen, he arrived at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 季述遣養子希度詣全忠，許以唐社稷輸之；

translations.literal: Jishu sent his adopted son Xidu to Quanzhong, promising to deliver the Tang altar and grain to him;
translations.idiomatic: Jishu sent his adopted son Xidu to Quanzhong, offering to surrender the Tang throne to him;

sentences.zh: 又遣供奉官李奉本以太上皇誥示全忠。

translations.literal: he also sent the palace attendant Li Fengben to show Quanzhong the retired emperor's proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: and sent palace attendant Li Fengben with a proclamation from the retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 全忠猶豫未決，會僚佐議之，或曰：「朝廷大事，非籓鎮所宜預知。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong hesitated undecided; his staff assembled to discuss it; someone said: "Great affairs of the court are not what a frontier command ought to foreknow."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong hesitated. His staff debated, and one adviser said: "Imperial affairs are none of a frontier lord's business."

sentences.zh: 天平節度副使李振獨曰：「王室有難，此霸者之資也。

translations.literal: Li Zhen, deputy commissioner of the Tianping circuit, alone said: "The royal house has difficulty—this is capital for a hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: Tianping deputy commissioner Li Zhen alone said: "When the throne is in peril, that is a hegemon's opportunity.

sentences.zh: 今公為唐桓、文，安危所屬。

translations.literal: Now you, sir, are for Tang what Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Jin were—the safety and peril depend upon you.
translations.idiomatic: You could be Tang's Duke Huan or Duke Wen—the realm's fate rests with you.

sentences.zh: 季述一宦豎耳，乃敢囚廢天子，公不能討，何以復令諸侯！

translations.literal: Jishu is only one eunuch lackey—yet he dares imprison and depose the Son of Heaven; if you, sir, cannot punish him, how can you again command the lords!
translations.idiomatic: Jishu is only a eunuch, yet he dares depose the emperor. If you cannot punish him, how can you command the lords?

sentences.zh: 且幼主位定，則天下之權盡歸宦官矣，是以太阿之柄授人也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, once the young sovereign's position is settled, then all power in the realm will entirely revert to the eunuchs—is this not handing over the hilt of the Great Awe sword to others?"
translations.idiomatic: And once the young emperor is secure, the eunuchs will hold all power—you will have handed them the sword."

sentences.zh: 全忠大悟，即囚希度、奉本，遣振如京師詗事。

translations.literal: Quanzhong greatly understood; immediately he imprisoned Xidu and Fengben, and sent Zhen to the capital to reconnoiter affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong saw the point at once. He imprisoned Xidu and Fengben and sent Zhen to the capital to scout the situation.

sentences.zh: 即還，又遣親吏蔣玄暉如京師，與崔胤謀之；

translations.literal: When he returned, he also sent his intimate officer Jiang Xuanhui to the capital to plot with Cui Yin;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen returned, Quanzhong sent his trusted officer Jiang Xuanhui to the capital to conspire with Cui Yin;

sentences.zh: 又召程巖赴大梁。

translations.literal: he also summoned Cheng Yan to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: and summoned Cheng Yan to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 清海節度使薛王知柔薨。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xue, military commissioner of Qinghai, Zhi Rourou, died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Rourou, Prince of Xue and military commissioner of Qinghai, died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，加楊行密兼侍中。

translations.literal: That year, Yang Xingmi was additionally granted the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yang Xingmi was also made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 睦州刺史陳晟卒，弟詢自稱刺史。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng, prefect of Muzhou, died; his younger brother Xun proclaimed himself prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhou prefect Chen Sheng died, and his brother Xun declared himself prefect.

sentences.zh: 太子即位累旬，籓鎮箋表多不至。

translations.literal: The crown prince had been on the throne for more than ten days; memorial letters from frontier commands mostly had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days after the new emperor's accession, most frontier commands had still not sent congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 王仲先性苛察，素知左、右軍多積弊，及為中尉，鉤校軍中錢穀，得隱沒為奸者，痛捶之，急征所負，將士頗不安。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongxian by nature was harsh and scrutinizing; he had long known that the Left and Right Armies accumulated many hidden abuses; once he became commander, he audited the army's funds and grain; those found concealing and committing fraud were beaten severely; he urgently collected what was owed—the officers and soldiers were quite unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongxian was harsh and knew the Left and Right Armies were riddled with graft. As commander he audited their accounts, beat those who had embezzled funds, and demanded immediate repayment—the troops grew restless.

sentences.zh: 有鹽州雄毅軍使孫德昭為左神策指揮使，自劉季述等廢立，常憤惋不平。

translations.literal: There was Sun Dezhao, commissioner of the Xiongyi Army of Yanzhou, serving as Left Shence commander—since Liu Jishu and the others deposed and installed rulers, he was often indignant and resentful, not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Dezhao, Xiongyi Army commissioner of Yanzhou and Left Shence commander, had been bitter since Jishu's coup.

sentences.zh: 崔胤聞之，遣判官石戩與之遊。

translations.literal: Cui Yin heard of this and sent his registrar Shi Yan to associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, Cui Yin sent registrar Shi Yan to cultivate his friendship.

sentences.zh: 德昭每酒酣必泣，戩知其誠，乃密以胤意說之曰：「自上皇幽閉，中外大臣至於行間士卒，孰不切齒！

translations.literal: Whenever Dezhao was deep in wine he inevitably wept; Yan knew his sincerity and secretly conveyed Yin's intent, saying to him: "Since the retired emperor was confined in seclusion, from grand ministers within and without down to common soldiers in the ranks—who does not gnash teeth!
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao wept whenever he drank. Yan saw his sincerity and privately relayed Yin's message: "Since the retired emperor was imprisoned, everyone from court ministers to common soldiers has gnashed their teeth in rage!

sentences.zh: 今反者獨季述、仲先耳，公誠能誅此二人，迎上皇復位，則富貴窮一時，忠義流千古；

translations.literal: Now the rebels are only Jishu and Zhongxian; if you, sir, can truly execute these two men and welcome the retired emperor to restore his position, then wealth and honor will exhaust one lifetime, but loyalty and righteousness will flow through a thousand ages;
translations.idiomatic: Only Jishu and Zhongxian are the traitors. If you kill them and restore the retired emperor, you will enjoy riches in this life and glory forever after;

sentences.zh: 苟狐疑不決，則功落他人之手矣！」

translations.literal: if you hesitatingly do not decide, then the merit will fall into another's hands!"
translations.idiomatic: Hesitate, and someone else will seize the credit!"

sentences.zh: 德昭謝曰：「德昭小校，國家大事，安敢專之！

translations.literal: Dezhao declined saying: "Dezhao is a petty officer—great affairs of state, how dare I monopolize them!
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao replied: "I am only a lowly officer—how dare I take it upon myself to decide the fate of the realm!

sentences.zh: 苟相公有命，不敢愛死！」

translations.literal: If the prime minister has orders, I dare not spare death!"
translations.idiomatic: But if the Chancellor commands it, I will not shrink from death!"

sentences.zh: 戩以白胤。

translations.literal: Yan reported this to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yan reported back to Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤割衣帶，手書以授之。

translations.literal: Yin cut his belt sash and with his own hand wrote and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin cut off his belt sash, wrote a message by hand, and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 德昭復結右軍清遠都將董彥弼、周承誨，謀以除夜伏兵安福門外以俟之。

translations.literal: Dezhao again joined with Dong Yanbi and Zhou Chenghui, commanders of the Qingyuan contingent of the Right Army, plotting on New Year's Eve to lie in ambush outside the Anfu Gate and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao then enlisted Right Army Qingyuan commanders Dong Yanbi and Zhou Chenghui and planned to ambush outside the Anfu Gate on New Year's Eve.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝中之中天復元年（

translations.literal: Middle of the reign of Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, and Filially Pious—first year of Tianfu (
translations.idiomatic: Reign of Emperor Zhaozong—middle period, first year of Tianfu (

sentences.zh: 辛酉，公元九零一年）

translations.literal: xinyou, corresponding to 901 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinyou, equivalent to 901 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉朔，王仲先入朝，至安福門，孫德昭擒斬之，馳詣少陽院，叩門呼曰：「逆賊已誅，請陛下出勞將士。」

translations.literal: Spring, first month, first day yiyou, Wang Zhongxian entered court; reaching the Anfu Gate, Sun Dezhao seized and beheaded him, galloped to the Shaoyang Courtyard, knocked on the gate and called: "The rebel traitors have been executed—please Your Majesty come out to comfort the officers and soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, Wang Zhongxian came to court. At the Anfu Gate Sun Dezhao seized and killed him, then raced to the Shaoyang Courtyard and knocked, shouting: "The traitors are dead—please come out, Your Majesty, and reward the troops!"

sentences.zh: 何-{后}-不信，曰：「果爾，以其首來！」

translations.literal: Empress He did not believe it, saying: "If it is truly so, bring his head!"
translations.idiomatic: Empress He refused to believe him: "If that is true, bring me his head!"

sentences.zh: 德昭獻其首，上乃與-{后}-毀扉而出。

translations.literal: Dezhao presented his head; the emperor then with the {empress} smashed the door and came out.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao brought them the head, and the emperor and the {empress} broke down the door and emerged.

sentences.zh: 崔胤迎上御長樂門樓，帥百官稱賀。

translations.literal: Cui Yin welcomed the emperor to ascend the Changle Gate tower, leading the hundred officials in offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin escorted the emperor to the Changle Gate tower and led the officials in congratulating him.

sentences.zh: 周承誨擒劉季述、王彥範繼至，方詰責，已為亂梃所斃。

translations.literal: Zhou Chenghui, having captured Liu Jishu and Wang Yanfan, arrived in succession; just as he was questioning and rebuking them, they were already beaten to death by riot clubs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chenghui arrived with Liu Jishu and Wang Yanfan in custody; before he could even finish questioning them, a mob clubbed them to death.

sentences.zh: 薛齊偓赴井死，出而斬之。

translations.literal: Xue Qiwo threw himself into a well to die; they pulled him out and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Qiwo drowned himself in a well; they fished him out and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 滅四人之族，並誅其黨二十餘人。

translations.literal: The clans of the four men were exterminated, and more than twenty of their partisans were also executed.
translations.idiomatic: The four men's entire clans were wiped out, along with more than twenty of their followers.

sentences.zh: 宦官奉太子匿於左軍，獻傳國寶。

translations.literal: The eunuchs escorted the crown prince and hid him in the Left Army, presenting the imperial seal of state.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs brought the crown prince to the Left Army for protection and surrendered the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「裕幼弱，為凶豎所立，非其罪也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yu is young and weak; he was installed by wicked villains—it is not his crime."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Yu is only a child. The villains put him on the throne—he is not to blame."

sentences.zh: 命還東宮，黜為德王，復名裕。

translations.literal: He ordered him returned to the Eastern Palace, demoted to Prince of De, and his name restored to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the boy sent back to the Eastern Palace, stripped of the crown prince title and made Prince of De, with his name restored to Yu.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以孫德昭同平章事，充靜海節度使，賜姓名李繼昭。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Sun Dezhao was made Grand Councilor and appointed military commissioner of Jinghai; he was granted the surname Li and the name Jizhao.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Sun Dezhao was made Grand Councilor and military commissioner of Jinghai, and given the surname Li and the name Jizhao.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，崔胤進位司徒，胤固辭。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Cui Yin was promoted to Minister of Education; Yin firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Cui Yin was promoted to Minister of Education, but he firmly refused the honor.

sentences.zh: 上寵待胤益厚。

translations.literal: The emperor favored and treated Yin with ever greater generosity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showered Yin with even greater favor.

sentences.zh: 己丑，朱全忠聞劉季述等誅，折程巖足，械送京師，並劉希度、李奉本等皆斬於都市，由是益重李振。

translations.literal: On jichou, Zhu Quanzhong, hearing that Liu Jishu and the others had been executed, broke Cheng Yan's legs, sent him in fetters to the capital, and together with Liu Xidu, Li Fengben, and others had them all beheaded in the marketplace; from this he valued Li Zhen all the more.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, learning that Liu Jishu and his co-conspirators were dead, Zhu Quanzhong had Cheng Yan's legs broken and sent him in chains to the capital; Liu Xidu, Li Fengben, and the rest were beheaded in the marketplace as well. From then on Zhu Quanzhong relied on Li Zhen even more heavily.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以周承誨為嶺南西道節度使，賜姓名李繼誨，董彥弼為寧遠節度，賜姓李，並同平章事；

translations.literal: On gengyin, Zhou Chenghui was made military commissioner of Lingnan West Circuit, granted the surname Li and the name Jihui; Dong Yanbi was made military commissioner of Ningyuan, granted the surname Li, and both were made Grand Councilors;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Zhou Chenghui was made military commissioner of Lingnan West Circuit and given the surname Li and the name Jihui; Dong Yanbi was made military commissioner of Ningyuan, granted the surname Li, and both were made Grand Councilors;

sentences.zh: 與李繼昭俱留宿衛，十日乃出還家，賞賜傾府庫，時人謂之「三使相」。

translations.literal: Together with Li Jizhao they all remained on palace guard duty; only after ten days did they leave and return home, rewards draining the treasury—people of the time called them "the Three Envoy-Chancellors."
translations.idiomatic: They and Li Jizhao remained on palace guard duty for ten days before returning home, their rewards emptying the treasury; contemporaries dubbed them "the Three Envoy-Chancellors."

sentences.zh: 癸巳，進朱全忠爵東平王。

translations.literal: On guisi, Zhu Quanzhong was advanced in rank to Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Zhu Quanzhong was ennobled as Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 丙午，敕：「近年宰臣延英奏事，樞密使侍側，爭論紛然。

translations.literal: On bingwu, an edict: "In recent years when chancellors presented business in the Yanying Hall, the commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs stood at their side, and disputes arose in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, an edict declared: "In recent years, when chancellors reported to the throne in the Yanying Hall, commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs stood at their side and wrangled over every decision.

sentences.zh: 既出，又稱上旨未允，復有改易，橈權亂政。

translations.literal: After leaving, they would again claim the emperor's intent had not been granted and make further changes, usurping authority and disrupting government.
translations.idiomatic: After the chancellors left, the commissioners would claim the emperor had not approved the decision and revise it—usurping power and sowing chaos in government.

sentences.zh: 自今並依大中舊制，俟宰臣奏事畢，方得升殿承受公事。」

translations.literal: From now on all shall follow the old Dazhong system: only after the chancellors have finished presenting business may they ascend the hall to receive official business."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the old Dazhong practice shall be restored: commissioners may enter the hall to receive official business only after the chancellors have finished their audience."

sentences.zh: 賜兩軍副使李師虔、徐彥孫自盡，皆劉季述之黨也。

translations.literal: Li Shiqian and Xu Yansun, deputy commissioners of the Two Armies, were granted permission to take their own lives—both were partisans of Liu Jishu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiqian and Xu Yansun, deputy commissioners of the Two Armies, were ordered to commit suicide; both had been Liu Jishu's allies.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔、彰義節度使李茂貞來朝；

translations.literal: Li Maozhen, military commissioner of Fengxiang and Zhangyi, came to court;
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen, military commissioner of Fengxiang and Zhangyi, came to court;

sentences.zh: 加茂貞守尚書令，兼侍中，進爵岐王。

translations.literal: Maozhen was additionally made acting Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Palace Secretary, and advanced in rank to Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen was made acting Director of the Department of State Affairs and Palace Secretary, and ennobled as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 劉季述、王仲先既死，崔胤、陸扆上言：「禍亂之興，皆由中官典兵。

translations.literal: After Liu Jishu and Wang Zhongxian had died, Cui Yin and Lu Yi submitted a memorial: "The rise of calamity and disorder all stems from eunuchs holding command of armies.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jishu and Wang Zhongxian were dead, Cui Yin and Lu Yi memorialized the throne: "Every recent disaster has come from eunuchs commanding the armies.

sentences.zh: 乞令胤主左軍，扆主右軍，則諸侯不敢侵陵，王室尊矣。」

translations.literal: We beg that Yin be put in charge of the Left Army and Yi of the Right Army—then the feudal lords will not dare encroach, and the royal house will be honored."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Yin be given command of the Left Army and Yi of the Right Army. Then the regional lords will not dare encroach, and the throne will stand secure."

sentences.zh: 上猶豫兩日未決。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated for two days without deciding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wavered for two days and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞聞之，怒曰：「崔胤奪軍權未得，已欲翦滅諸侯！」

translations.literal: Li Maozhen heard of it and angrily said: "Cui Yin has not yet even seized military power, and already he wants to cut down the feudal lords!"
translations.idiomatic: When Li Maozhen heard of this, he fumed: "Cui Yin hasn't even seized the armies yet, and already he wants to destroy the regional lords!"

sentences.zh: 上召李繼昭、李繼誨、李彥弼謀之，皆曰：「臣等累世在軍中，未聞書生為軍主；

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Li Jizhao, Li Jihui, and Li Yanbi to consult them; all said: "We have served in the armies for generations and have never heard of a scholar as army commander;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Li Jizhao, Li Jihui, and Li Yanbi for counsel. All three said: "Our families have served in the armies for generations—we have never seen a scholar put in command;

sentences.zh: 若屬南司，必多所變更，不若歸之北司為便。」

translations.literal: If entrusted to the Southern Office, there will surely be many changes—it would be better to return it to the Northern Office."
translations.idiomatic: If the armies fall to the civil officials, everything will change. Better to leave them with the eunuchs."

sentences.zh: 上乃謂胤、扆曰：「將士意不欲屬文臣，卿曹勿堅求。」

translations.literal: The emperor then said to Yin and Yi: "The officers and soldiers do not wish to be under civil officials—you two must not insist."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then told Yin and Yi: "The troops do not want civil officials in command. Do not press the matter."

sentences.zh: 於是以樞密使韓全誨、鳳翔監軍使張彥弘為左、右中尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs Han Quanhui and the Fengxiang army supervisor Zhang Yanhong were made Left and Right Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, Han Quanhui, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Zhang Yanhong, Fengxiang army supervisor, were made Left and Right Commandants.

sentences.zh: 全誨亦前鳳翔監軍也。

translations.literal: Quanhui was also a former Fengxiang army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui had also once served as Fengxiang army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 又征前樞密使致仕嚴遵美為兩軍中尉、觀軍容處置使。

translations.literal: The former commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the retired Yan Zunmei, was also summoned to be Commandant of the Two Armies and Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zunmei, a former commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs now in retirement, was also summoned to serve as Commandant of the Two Armies and Army Commander.

sentences.zh: 遵美曰：「一軍猶不可為，況兩軍乎！」

translations.literal: Zunmei said: "One army is still not something one can manage—how much less two armies!"
translations.idiomatic: Zunmei replied: "I could not manage even one army—how could I manage two!"

sentences.zh: 固辭不起。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and would not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused and would not take the appointment.

sentences.zh: 以袁易簡、周敬容為樞密使。

translations.literal: Yuan Yijian and Zhou Jingrong were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yijian and Zhou Jingrong were appointed commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞辭還鎮。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen took leave and returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen took his leave and returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 崔胤以宦官典兵，終為肘腋之患，欲以外兵制之，諷茂貞留兵三千於京師，充宿衛，以茂貞假子繼筠將之。

translations.literal: Cui Yin, considering that eunuchs holding command of armies would ultimately be a danger close at hand, wished to use outside troops to control them; he hinted to Maozhen to leave three thousand troops in the capital as palace guards, with Maozhen's adopted son Jiyun to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin feared that eunuch control of the armies would forever be a threat at his elbow and wanted outside troops to counterbalance them. He urged Maozhen to leave three thousand men in the capital as palace guards under Maozhen's adopted son Jiyun.

sentences.zh: 左諫議大夫萬年韓偓以為不可，胤曰：「兵自不肯去，非留之也。」

translations.literal: Han Wo of Wannian, Left Remonstrance Censor, considered it inadvisable; Yin said: "The troops themselves are unwilling to leave—it is not that we are keeping them."
translations.idiomatic: Han Wo of Wannian, Left Remonstrance Censor, argued against it. Yin replied: "The troops refuse to leave on their own—we are not forcing them to stay."

sentences.zh: 偓曰：「始者何為召之邪？」

translations.literal: Wo said: "Then why summon them in the first place?"
translations.idiomatic: Han Wo asked: "Then why did you summon them here in the first place?"

sentences.zh: 胤無以應。

translations.literal: Yin had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had no answer.
