sentences.zh: 偓曰：「留此兵則家國兩危，不留則家國兩安。」

translations.literal: Wo said: "Keep these troops and both house and state are in danger; do not keep them and both house and state are secure."
translations.idiomatic: Han Wo said: "Keep these troops and both throne and realm are endangered; send them away and both are safe."

sentences.zh: 胤不從。

translations.literal: Yin did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yin would not listen.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠既服河北，欲先取河中以制河東。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong, having already subdued Hebei, wished first to take Hezhong to control Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong, having subdued Hebei, planned to seize Hezhong first and thereby pin down Hedong.

sentences.zh: 己亥，召諸將謂曰：「王珂駑材，恃太原自驕汰。

translations.literal: On jihai, he summoned his generals and said: "Wang Ke is a mediocre talent who relies on Taiyuan and is arrogant and extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he summoned his generals and said: "Wang Ke is a mediocrity who struts on Taiyuan's backing.

sentences.zh: 吾今斷長蛇之腰，諸君為我以一繩縛之。」

translations.literal: I will now cut the long serpent in half at the waist—you gentlemen, bind it for me with a single rope."
translations.idiomatic: I am about to cut the long serpent in two at the waist. Gentlemen, bind it for me with a single rope."

sentences.zh: 庚子，遣張存敬將兵三萬自汜水度河出捨山路以襲之，全忠以中軍繼其後。

translations.literal: On gengzi, he dispatched Zhang Cunjing leading thirty thousand troops to cross the river at Sishui and emerge by the Sheshan route to strike; Quanzhong followed with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he sent Zhang Cunjing with thirty thousand men to cross the Yellow River at Sishui and strike along the Sheshan route, while Quanzhong followed with the main force.

sentences.zh: 戊申，存敬至絳州。

translations.literal: On wushen, Cunjing reached Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Cunjing reached Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晉、絳不意其至，皆無守備，庚戌，絳州刺史陶建釗降之；

translations.literal: Jin and Jiang did not expect his arrival and had no defenses; on gengxu, Jiang Prefecture governor Tao Jianzhao surrendered to him;
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Jiang were caught unprepared and had no defenses in place. On gengxu, Jiang Prefecture governor Tao Jianzhao surrendered;

sentences.zh: 壬子，晉州刺史張漢瑜降之。

translations.literal: On renzi, Jin Prefecture governor Zhang Hanyu surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Jin Prefecture governor Zhang Hanyu surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣其將侯言守晉州，何絪守絳州，屯兵二萬以扼河東援兵之路。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent his generals Hou Yan to hold Jin Prefecture and He Yin to hold Jiang Prefecture, stationing twenty thousand troops to block the route of Hedong relief forces.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong left Hou Yan to hold Jin Prefecture and He Yin to hold Jiang Prefecture, with twenty thousand men posted to block Hedong relief columns.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恐全忠西入關，急賜詔和解之；

translations.literal: The court, fearing Quanzhong would enter the passes to the west, urgently issued an edict to mediate and reconcile;
translations.idiomatic: The court, fearing Quanzhong would drive west through the passes, urgently issued an edict calling for peace;

sentences.zh: 全忠不從。

translations.literal: Quanzhong did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong ignored it.

sentences.zh: 珂遣間使告急於李克用，道路相繼，克用以汴人先據晉、絳，兵不得進。

translations.literal: Ke sent secret envoys in succession along the road to report the emergency to Li Keyong; Keyong, because the Bian troops had already seized Jin and Jiang, could not advance his army.
translations.idiomatic: Ke sent secret messengers one after another to Li Keyong begging for help, but Keyong could not move—Bian forces already held Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 珂妻遺克用書曰：「兒旦暮為俘虜，大人何忍不救！」

translations.literal: Ke's wife sent a letter to Keyong saying: "Our son will soon be taken captive morning and evening—how can Your Highness bear not to save him!"
translations.idiomatic: Ke's wife wrote to Keyong: "Our son will be a prisoner any day now—how can you stand by and do nothing!"

sentences.zh: 克用報曰：「今賊兵塞晉、絳，眾寡不敵，進則與汝兩亡，不若與王郎舉族歸朝。」

translations.literal: Keyong replied: "Now the rebel troops block Jin and Jiang; our numbers cannot match theirs—advance and both you perish together. Better to have Lord Wang bring his whole clan back to court."
translations.idiomatic: Keyong replied: "The enemy holds Jin and Jiang. We are outnumbered—if I advance, you and I both die. Better that Lord Wang bring his whole clan to court and submit."

sentences.zh: 珂又遺李茂貞書，言：「天子新返正，詔籓鎮無得相攻，同獎王室。

translations.literal: Ke also sent a letter to Li Maozhen, saying: "The Son of Heaven has newly returned to the throne; an edict forbids the frontier commands from attacking one another and calls on all to support the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Ke also wrote to Li Maozhen: "The emperor has just been restored. The throne has ordered the regional commands not to attack one another but to rally to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 今諸公不顧詔命，首興兵相加，其心可見。

translations.literal: Now the lords disregard the edict and are first to raise arms against each other—their intent is plain to see.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you lords ignore that edict and strike first at one another—the design is obvious.

sentences.zh: 河中若亡，則同華、邠、岐俱不自保。

translations.literal: If Hezhong falls, then Tonghua, Bin, and Qi will none of them be able to preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If Hezhong falls, Tonghua, Bin, and Qi will none of them survive.

sentences.zh: 天子神器拱手授人，其勢必然矣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's sacred regalia will be handed over with folded arms—the trend is inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: The throne itself will be surrendered without a fight—that is where this leads.

sentences.zh: 公宜亟帥關中諸鎮兵，固守潼關，赴救河中。

translations.literal: Your Lordship should urgently lead the troops of the Guanzhong commands, firmly hold Tong Pass, and hurry to rescue Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: You should immediately lead the Guanzhong commands to hold Tong Pass and march to Hezhong's relief.

sentences.zh: 僕自知不武，願於公西偏授一小鎮，此地請公有之。

translations.literal: I know myself to be no warrior; I wish only that Your Lordship grant me a small command on your western flank—this territory I ask Your Lordship to take for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: I know I am no fighter. Grant me some small post on your western flank, and take Hezhong for yourself.

sentences.zh: 關中安危，國祚修短，系公此舉，願審思之！」

translations.literal: The safety of Guanzhong and the length of the dynasty's fortune hang on this act of Your Lordship—I beg you consider it carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: The fate of Guanzhong and the dynasty itself rests on what you do now. Think hard before you decide!"

sentences.zh: 茂貞素無遠圖，不報。

translations.literal: Maozhen had never had far-reaching plans and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen had never been a man of vision. He did not answer.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲寅朔，河東將李嗣昭攻澤州，拔之。

translations.literal: Second month, first day jiayin, Hedong general Li Sizhao attacked Ze Prefecture and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day, Hedong general Li Sizhao attacked Ze Prefecture and took it.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，張存敬引兵發晉州；

translations.literal: On yimao, Zhang Cunjing led troops out from Jin Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Zhang Cunjing marched out from Jin Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 己未，至河中，遂圍之。

translations.literal: On jiwei, he reached Hezhong and thereupon besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei he reached Hezhong and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 王珂勢窮，將奔京師，而人心離貳，會浮梁壞，流澌塞河，舟行甚難，珂挈其族數百人欲夜登舟，親諭守城者，皆不應。

translations.literal: Wang Ke's situation was desperate; he was about to flee to the capital, but hearts were divided and disloyal. By chance the pontoon bridge was broken and ice floes blocked the river, making travel by boat very difficult. Ke took several hundred of his clan intending to board boats by night; he personally addressed the city defenders, but none responded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke was cornered and planned to flee to the capital, but morale had collapsed. The pontoon bridge was broken and ice floes choked the river, making escape by boat nearly impossible. Ke gathered several hundred kinsmen to slip away by night and pleaded personally with the garrison, but no one would follow.

sentences.zh: 牙將劉訓曰：「今人情擾擾，若夜出涉河，必爭舟紛亂，一夫作難，事不可知。

translations.literal: Garrison officer Liu Xun said: "Now hearts are agitated and unsettled; if we go out by night to cross the river, there will surely be scrambling for boats in disorder—if one man makes trouble, the outcome cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison officer Liu Xun said: "The men are already panicking. If we try to cross the river by night, they'll fight over the boats—and one troublemaker could wreck everything.

sentences.zh: 不若且送款存敬，徐圖向背。」

translations.literal: Better to submit terms to Cunjing for now and slowly plan which way to turn."
translations.idiomatic: Better to offer terms to Cunjing for now and watch how things develop."

sentences.zh: 珂從之。

translations.literal: Ke followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Ke agreed.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，珂植白幡於城隅，遣使以牌印請降於存敬。

translations.literal: On renxu, Ke planted a white banner at a corner of the wall and sent envoys with his seal and tally to request surrender to Cunjing.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Ke raised a white flag on the city wall and sent envoys with his seal and tally to surrender to Cunjing.

sentences.zh: 存敬請開城，珂曰：「吾於朱公有家世事分，請公退捨，俟朱公至，吾自以城授之。」

translations.literal: Cunjing asked him to open the city; Ke said: "I have a family bond of generations with Lord Zhu—please withdraw your camp and wait until Lord Zhu arrives; I myself will hand the city over to him."
translations.idiomatic: Cunjing asked him to open the gates. Ke replied: "My family and Lord Zhu's go back generations. Please withdraw your camp and wait for Lord Zhu—I will surrender the city to him myself."

sentences.zh: 存敬從之，且使走白全忠。

translations.literal: Cunjing complied and also sent a runner to inform Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjing agreed and sent a messenger racing to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，全忠至洛陽，聞之喜，馳往赴之。

translations.literal: On yichou, Quanzhong reached Luoyang; hearing the news he rejoiced and galloped to go there.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Quanzhong reached Luoyang. Delighted at the news, he galloped straight for Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，至虞鄉，先哭於重榮之墓，盡哀；

translations.literal: On wuchen, reaching Yuxiang, he first wept at Chongrong's tomb with full grief;
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he reached Yuxiang and first wept at Chongrong's tomb with full mourning;

sentences.zh: 河中人皆悅。

translations.literal: The people of Hezhong were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: the people of Hezhong were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 珂欲面縛牽羊出迎，全忠遽使止之曰：「太師舅之恩何可忘！

translations.literal: Ke wished to come out bound and leading a sheep in submission; Quanzhong hurriedly sent word to stop him, saying: "How can the grace of the Grand Preceptor, your maternal uncle, be forgotten!
translations.idiomatic: Ke wanted to come out bound and leading a sheep in surrender. Quanzhong stopped him at once: "How can I forget the kindness of the Grand Preceptor, your uncle by marriage!

sentences.zh: 若郎君如此，使僕異日何以見舅於九泉！」

translations.literal: If the young lord acts thus, how shall I ever face my uncle in the nine springs hereafter!"
translations.idiomatic: If you humiliate yourself like this, how will I ever face my uncle in the grave!"

sentences.zh: 乃以常禮出迎，握手歔欷，聯轡入城。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ke came out to welcome him with ordinary ceremony; they clasped hands, weeping, and entered the city riding side by side.
translations.idiomatic: Ke came out to greet him with ordinary courtesy. They clasped hands, weeping, and rode into the city side by side.

sentences.zh: 全忠表張存敬為護國軍留後，王珂舉族遷於大梁。

translations.literal: Quanzhong memorialized Zhang Cunjing as acting military commissioner of Huguo Army; Wang Ke moved his whole clan to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong recommended Zhang Cunjing as acting military commissioner of the Huguo Army and relocated Wang Ke's entire clan to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 其後全忠遣珂入朝，遣人殺之於華州。

translations.literal: Afterward Quanzhong sent Ke to court and dispatched men to kill him at Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later Quanzhong sent Ke to court, then had him murdered at Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 全忠聞張夫人疾亟，遽自河中東歸。

translations.literal: Quanzhong heard that Lady Zhang's illness was critical and hurriedly returned east from Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong learned that Lady Zhang was gravely ill, he raced back east from Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 李克用遣使以重幣請修好於全忠；

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent envoys with heavy gifts to request reconciliation with Quanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent envoys bearing lavish gifts to sue for peace with Quanzhong;

sentences.zh: 全忠雖遣使報之，而忿其書辭蹇傲，決欲攻之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong though he sent envoys in reply, resented the arrogant tone of the letter and resolved to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent a reply, but the letter's haughty tone enraged him and he resolved to attack.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士、戶部侍郎王溥為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Pu was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Pu was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 以吏部侍郎裴樞為戶部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Pei Shu was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Pei Shu was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 溥，正雅之從孫也，常在崔胤幕府，故胤引之。

translations.literal: Pu was a grand-nephew of Zhengya; he had long been in Cui Yin's staff, and so Yin brought him forward.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was a grand-nephew of Zhengya and had long served on Cui Yin's staff; Yin had him promoted.

sentences.zh: 贈謚故睦王倚曰恭哀太子。

translations.literal: The posthumous title of the late Prince of Mu, Yi, was granted as Crown Prince Gong'ai.
translations.idiomatic: The late Prince of Mu, Yi, was posthumously honored as Crown Prince Gong'ai.

sentences.zh: 加幽州節度使劉仁恭、魏博節度使羅紹威並兼侍中。

translations.literal: You Prefecture military commissioner Liu Rengong and Weibo military commissioner Luo Shaowei were both additionally made Palace Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong, military commissioner of You Prefecture, and Luo Shaowei, military commissioner of Weibo, were both made Palace Secretaries as well.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸未朔，朱全忠至大梁。

translations.literal: Third month, first day guiwei, Zhu Quanzhong reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day, Zhu Quanzhong reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，遣氏叔琮等將兵五萬攻李克用，入自太行，魏博都將張文恭入自磁州新口，葛從周以兗、鄆兵會成德兵入自土門，洺州刺史張歸厚入自馬嶺，義武節度使王處直入自飛狐，權知晉州侯言以慈、隰、晉、絳兵入自陰地。

translations.literal: On guimao, Shi Shuzong and others were dispatched leading fifty thousand troops to attack Li Keyong, entering by the Taihang; Weibo capital guard general Zhang Wengong entered by the new crossing at Ci Prefecture; Ge Congzhou with Yan and Yun troops joined Chengde troops entering by Tumen; Ming Prefecture governor Zhang Guihou entered by Maling; Yiwu military commissioner Wang Churu entered by Feihu; acting Jin Prefecture governor Hou Yan with Ci, Xi, Jin, and Jiang troops entered by Yindi.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Quanzhong sent Shi Shuzong and others with fifty thousand men against Li Keyong. Shi entered through the Taihang range; Weibo capital guard general Zhang Wengong through the new crossing at Ci Prefecture; Ge Congzhou with Yan and Yun troops alongside Chengde forces through Tumen; Ming Prefecture governor Zhang Guihou through Maling; Yiwu military commissioner Wang Churu through Feihu; and acting Jin Prefecture governor Hou Yan with Ci, Xi, Jin, and Jiang troops through Yindi.

sentences.zh: 叔琮入天井關，進軍昂車。

translations.literal: Shuzong entered Tianjing Pass and advanced the army to Angche.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzong passed through Tianjing Pass and advanced to Angche.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，沁州刺史蔡訓以城降。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Qin Prefecture governor Cai Xun surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Qin Prefecture governor Cai Xun surrendered his city.

sentences.zh: 河東都將蓋璋詣侯言降，即令權知沁州。

translations.literal: Hedong capital guard general Gai Zhang went to Hou Yan and surrendered; he was immediately appointed acting governor of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong capital guard general Gai Zhang surrendered to Hou Yan and was immediately made acting governor of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬子，叔琮拔澤州，刺史李存璋棄城走。

translations.literal: On renzi, Shuzong captured Ze Prefecture; governor Li Cunzhang abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Shuzong took Ze Prefecture; governor Li Cunzhang abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 叔琮進攻潞州，昭義節度使孟遷降之。

translations.literal: Shuzong advanced to attack Lu Prefecture; Zhaoyi military commissioner Meng Qian surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzong pressed on to Lu Prefecture; Zhaoyi military commissioner Meng Qian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 河東屯將李審建、王周將步軍一萬、騎二千詣督琮降。

translations.literal: Hedong garrison generals Li Shenjian and Wang Zhou led ten thousand infantry and two thousand cavalry to Shuzong and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong garrison generals Li Shenjian and Wang Zhou came to Shuzong with ten thousand foot soldiers and two thousand cavalry and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 叔琮進趣晉陽。

translations.literal: Shuzong pressed on toward Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzong pressed on toward Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙卯，叔琮出石會關，營於洞渦驛。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on yimao, Shuzong emerged from Shihui Pass and encamped at Dongwo Post.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yimao, Shuzong came out through Shihui Pass and encamped at Dongwo Post.

sentences.zh: 張歸厚引兵至遼州，丁巳，遼州刺史張鄂降。

translations.literal: Zhang Guihou led troops to Liao Prefecture; on dingsi, Liao Prefecture governor Zhang E surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guihou marched to Liao Prefecture; on dingsi, Liao Prefecture governor Zhang E surrendered.

sentences.zh: 別將白奉國會成德兵自井陘入，己未，拔承天軍，與叔琮烽火相應。

translations.literal: Separate commander Bai Fengguo joined Chengde troops entering by Jingxing; on jiwei, they captured Chengtian Army and exchanged beacon signals with Shuzong.
translations.idiomatic: Separate commander Bai Fengguo joined Chengde troops coming through Jingxing; on jiwei they took Chengtian Army and exchanged beacon signals with Shuzong.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，上謁太廟。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the emperor visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the emperor paid homage at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On dingchou, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven and the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, the emperor declared a general amnesty and changed the reign era.

sentences.zh: 雪王涯等十七家。

translations.literal: The seventeen clans including Wang Ya were cleared of wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: The seventeen families implicated with Wang Ya were posthumously rehabilitated.

sentences.zh: 初，楊復恭為中尉，借度支賣曲之利一年以贍兩軍，自是不肯復歸。

translations.literal: Initially, when Yang Fugong was Commandant, he borrowed the revenue from the Revenue Bureau's monopoly on selling yeast for one year to support the Two Armies, and from then on refused to return it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yang Fugong served as Commandant, he had diverted one year's revenue from the state yeast monopoly to fund the Two Armies—and ever after refused to give it back.

sentences.zh: 至是，崔胤草赦，欲抑宦官，聽酤者自造曲，但月輸榷酤錢。

translations.literal: At this time, Cui Yin drafted the amnesty edict, wishing to restrain the eunuchs: brewers were permitted to make their own yeast but had only to pay the monthly monopoly tax on liquor.
translations.idiomatic: Now Cui Yin drafted the amnesty edict to curb the eunuchs: private brewers could make their own yeast, paying only the monthly liquor monopoly tax.

sentences.zh: 兩軍先所造曲，趣令減價賣之，過七月無得復賣。

translations.literal: The yeast the Two Armies had already made was ordered sold at reduced prices; after seven months it might not be sold again.
translations.idiomatic: Yeast stockpiled by the Two Armies had to be sold off at reduced prices, and after seven months none could be sold at all.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使王宗滌以疾求代，王建表馬步使王宗裕為留後。

translations.literal: Wang Zongdi, military commissioner of Dongchuan, requested replacement on grounds of illness; Wang Jian memorialized that infantry-and-cavalry commissioner Wang Zongyu be made acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongdi of Dongchuan asked to be relieved for illness; Wang Jian recommended infantry-and-cavalry commissioner Wang Zongyu as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 氏叔琮等引兵抵晉陽城下，數挑戰，城中大恐。

translations.literal: Shi Shuzong and others led troops to the walls of Jinyang, repeatedly offering battle; inside the city there was great terror.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shuzong and his commanders brought their army to the walls of Jinyang and taunted the garrison daily; panic spread through the city.

sentences.zh: 李克用登城備御，不遑飲食。

translations.literal: Li Keyong mounted the wall to prepare defenses, with no leisure for food or drink.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong took to the walls to direct the defense, barely stopping to eat or drink.

sentences.zh: 時大雨積旬，城多頹壞，隨加完補。

translations.literal: At the time heavy rain had lasted more than ten days; much of the wall had collapsed and was repaired as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Rain had fallen for weeks; sections of the wall kept collapsing and were patched as fast as crews could work.

sentences.zh: 河東將李嗣昭、李嗣源鑿暗門，夜出攻汴壘，屢有殺獲。

translations.literal: Hedong generals Li Sizhao and Li Siyuan cut secret sally ports, sallied by night to attack Bian camps, and repeatedly killed and captured the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong generals Li Sizhao and Li Siyuan opened hidden sally ports and raided Bian camps by night, repeatedly inflicting casualties.

sentences.zh: 李存進敗汴軍於洞渦。

translations.literal: Li Cunjin defeated Bian troops at Dongwo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunjin routed Bian forces at Dongwo.

sentences.zh: 時汴軍既眾，芻糧不給，久雨，士卒瘧利，全忠乃召兵還。

translations.literal: The Bian army was now numerous but fodder and grain could not be supplied; the long rain brought malaria and dysentery among the troops, and Quanzhong thereupon recalled his army.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian army had swelled beyond its supply lines; weeks of rain brought malaria and dysentery, and Quanzhong ordered a withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 五月，叔琮等自石會關歸，諸道軍亦退。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Shuzong and others returned through Shihui Pass, and the armies of the various circuits also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Shuzong marched back through Shihui Pass, and the other columns retreated as well.

sentences.zh: 河東將周德威、李嗣昭以精騎五千躡之，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Hedong generals Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao with five thousand elite cavalry pursued them, killing and capturing in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao of Hedong harried the retreat with five thousand elite cavalry, inflicting heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 先是，汾州刺史李瑭舉州附於汴軍，克用遣其將李存審攻之，三日而拔，執瑭，斬之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fen Prefecture governor Li Tang had surrendered his prefecture to the Bian army; Keyong sent his general Li Cunshen to attack, captured it in three days, seized Tang, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fen Prefecture governor Li Tang had defected to the Bian army. Keyong sent Li Cunshen, who took the city in three days, captured Tang, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 氏叔琮過上黨，孟遷挈族隨之南徙。

translations.literal: Shi Shuzong passed through Shangdang; Meng Qian took his clan and followed him south in migration.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Shuzong passed through Shangdang, Meng Qian moved his entire clan south with the Bian column.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣丁會代守潞州。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent Ding Hui to replace him in holding Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Ding Hui to hold Lu Prefecture in his stead.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠奏乞除河中節度使，而諷吏民請己為帥。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong memorialized requesting appointment as military commissioner of Hezhong, while prompting officials and commoners to ask that he be made commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong petitioned to be made military commissioner of Hezhong and quietly orchestrated local petitions naming him commander.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以全忠為宣武、宣義，天平、護國四鎮節度使。

translations.literal: On guimao, Quanzhong was made military commissioner of the four commands Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, and Huguo.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Quanzhong was made military commissioner of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, and Huguo—four commands at once.

sentences.zh: 己酉，加鎮海、鎮東節度使錢鏐守侍中。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Qian Liu, military commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong, was additionally made acting Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Qian Liu of Zhenhai and Zhendong was made acting Palace Secretary as well.

sentences.zh: 崔胤之罷兩軍賣麴也，並近鎮亦禁之。

translations.literal: When Cui Yin abolished the Two Armies' sale of yeast, nearby commands were also forbidden to sell it.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yin ended the Two Armies' yeast monopoly, neighboring commands were barred from selling yeast as well.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞惜其利，表乞入朝論奏，韓全誨請許之。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen regretted the loss of profit and memorialized begging to enter court to argue the matter; Han Quanhui asked that he be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen, loath to lose the revenue, petitioned to come to court and plead his case; Han Quanhui urged the emperor to allow it.

sentences.zh: 茂貞至京師，全誨深與相結。

translations.literal: When Maozhen reached the capital, Quanhui formed a deep alliance with him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Maozhen reached the capital, he and Quanhui became close allies.

sentences.zh: 崔胤始懼，陰厚朱全忠益甚，與茂貞為仇敵矣。

translations.literal: Cui Yin began to fear and secretly treated Zhu Quanzhong with ever greater generosity; he and Maozhen became bitter enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin grew alarmed and secretly lavished even more favor on Zhu Quanzhong; he and Maozhen were now sworn foes.

sentences.zh: 以佑國節度使張全義兼中書令。

translations.literal: Youguo military commissioner Zhang Quanyi was additionally made Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi, military commissioner of Youguo, was also made Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸亥，朱全忠如河中。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on guihai, Zhu Quanzhong went to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guihai, Zhu Quanzhong traveled to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 上之返正也，中書舍人令狐渙、給事中韓偓皆預其謀，故擢為翰林學士，數召對，訪以機密。

translations.literal: When the emperor was restored to the throne, Secretariat Drafter Linghu Huan and Supervising Censor Han Wo had both taken part in the plot, and so were promoted to Hanlin Academicians, repeatedly summoned for audience, and consulted on secret matters.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was restored, Secretariat Drafter Linghu Huan and Supervising Censor Han Wo—both conspirators in the coup—were made Hanlin Academicians and repeatedly summoned for confidential counsel.

sentences.zh: 渙，綯之子也。

translations.literal: Huan was the son of Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was a son of Linghu Tao.

sentences.zh: 時上悉以軍國事委崔胤，每奏事，上與之從容，或至然燭。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor entrusted all military and state affairs to Cui Yin; whenever Yin reported, the emperor spoke with him at ease, sometimes until the candles burned down.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor now entrusted all military and civil affairs to Cui Yin, talking with him at length after each audience—sometimes until the candles burned out.

sentences.zh: 宦官畏之側目，事無大小，皆咨胤而後行。

translations.literal: The eunuchs feared him and watched with sidelong glances; nothing great or small was done without consulting Yin first.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs watched in fear as Yin gained power; nothing was done until Yin had been consulted.

sentences.zh: 胤志欲盡除之，韓偓屢諫曰：「事禁太甚。

translations.literal: Yin was determined to eliminate them all; Han Wo repeatedly remonstrated, saying: "The matter is forbidden to go too far.
translations.idiomatic: Yin aimed to wipe them out entirely. Han Wo warned repeatedly: "You are going too far.

sentences.zh: 此輩亦不可全無，恐其黨迫切，更生他變。」

translations.literal: These people also cannot be entirely eliminated—for fear their faction, pressed hard, will produce other changes."
translations.idiomatic: You cannot eliminate them all—drive them to desperation and they will turn on you in new ways."

sentences.zh: 胤不從。

translations.literal: Yin did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yin would not listen.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，上獨召偓，問曰：「敕使中為惡者如林，何以處之？」

translations.literal: On dingmao, the emperor alone summoned Wo and asked: "Among the edict commissioners the wicked are like a forest—how are they to be dealt with?"
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the emperor summoned Wo alone and asked: "The edict commissioners are wicked beyond counting. What should I do with them?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「東內之難，敕使誰非同惡，處之當在正旦，今已失其時矣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "In the crisis of the Eastern Inner Palace, which edict commissioner was not equally guilty? The matter should have been handled at the very restoration—now the moment is lost."
translations.idiomatic: Wo replied: "Every edict commissioner was complicit in the Eastern Palace coup. That should have been settled the day you were restored—it is too late now."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「當是時，卿何不為崔胤言之？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "At that time, why did you not speak to Cui Yin about it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Then why didn't you tell Cui Yin?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣見陛下詔書雲，『自劉季述等四家之外，其餘一無所問。』

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject saw Your Majesty's edict saying, 'Apart from the four clans of Liu Jishu and the others, the rest shall not be questioned at all.'
translations.idiomatic: Wo replied: "I saw Your Majesty's edict: 'Beyond the four clans of Liu Jishu and his co-conspirators, no one else shall be punished.'

sentences.zh: 夫人主所重，莫大於信，既下此詔，則守之宜堅。

translations.literal: Nothing a ruler holds dear is greater than trust; once this edict was issued, it should be kept firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing matters more to a ruler than keeping his word. Once that edict went out, you had to stand by it.

sentences.zh: 若復戮一人，則人人懼死矣。

translations.literal: If one more person is executed, then every man will fear death.
translations.idiomatic: Execute one more man and everyone will fear for his life.

sentences.zh: 然後來所去者已為不少，此其所以忷忷不安也。

translations.literal: Yet afterward those removed have already been no few in number—this is why they are agitated and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: And since then you have removed quite a few anyway—that is why they are so restless and afraid.

sentences.zh: 陛下不若擇其尤無良者數人，明示其罪，置之於法，然後撫諭其餘曰：『吾恐爾曹謂吾心有所貯，自今可無疑矣。』

translations.literal: Your Majesty would do better to choose several of the most wicked, openly show their crimes, and punish them by law; then comfort and instruct the rest, saying: 'I fear you think my heart harbors resentment—from now on you need have no doubt.'
translations.idiomatic: Better to pick out the worst few, expose their crimes, and punish them by law. Then reassure the rest: 'I know you fear I still bear a grudge—from now on, put your minds at ease.'

sentences.zh: 乃擇其忠厚者使為之長。

translations.literal: Then choose the loyal and honest among them and make them leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Then appoint the trustworthy ones as their leaders.

sentences.zh: 其徒有善則獎之，有罪則懲之，咸自安矣。

translations.literal: Reward their followers when they do good and punish them when they commit offenses—all will settle themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Reward good conduct and punish wrongdoing, and they will all calm down.

sentences.zh: 今此曹在公私者以萬數，豈可盡誅邪！

translations.literal: Now these people in public and private service number in the tens of thousands—how could they all be executed!
translations.idiomatic: There are tens of thousands of them in government service—you cannot kill them all!

sentences.zh: 夫帝王之道，當以重厚鎮之，公正御之，至於瑣細機巧，此機生則彼機應矣，終不能成大功，所謂理絲而棼之者也。

translations.literal: The way of emperors and kings should use weight and magnanimity to stabilize, and fairness to govern; as for petty tricks and schemes—one scheme arises and another answers it—ultimately no great achievement can be made. This is what is called combing silk only to tangle it.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler should govern with weight and magnanimity, with fairness and steadiness. Petty scheming only breeds counter-scheming and never achieves anything lasting—it is like combing silk only to tangle it worse.

sentences.zh: 況今朝廷之權，散在四方。

translations.literal: Moreover, the court's authority today is scattered among the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: And today imperial power is scattered across the realm.

sentences.zh: 苟能先收此權，則事無不可為者矣。

translations.literal: If this authority can first be gathered in, then nothing cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Gather that power back first, and nothing will be impossible.

sentences.zh: ?鄙仙鉅暈□滑曰：「此事終以屬卿。」

translations.literal: [Text corrupt] said: "This matter will ultimately fall to you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said to him: "In the end, this will be your responsibility."

sentences.zh: 李克用遣其將李嗣昭、周德威將兵出陰地關，攻隰州，刺史唐禮降之。

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent his generals Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei leading troops out through Yindi Pass to attack Xi Prefecture; governor Tang Li surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei through Yindi Pass against Xi Prefecture; governor Tang Li surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進攻慈州，刺史張瑰降之。

translations.literal: They advanced to attack Ci Prefecture; governor Zhang Gui surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to Ci Prefecture; governor Zhang Gui surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 閏月，以河陽節度使丁會為昭義節度使，孟遷為河陽節度使，從朱全忠之請也。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Heyang military commissioner Ding Hui was made military commissioner of Zhaoyi, and Meng Qian was made military commissioner of Heyang—following Zhu Quanzhong's request.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, at Zhu Quanzhong's request, Ding Hui was moved from Heyang to Zhaoyi, and Meng Qian took Heyang.

sentences.zh: 道士杜從法以妖妄妄誘昌、普、合三州民作亂，王建遣行營兵馬使王宗黯將兵三萬會東川、武信兵討之。

translations.literal: The Daoist Du Congfa with wild delusion seduced the people of Chang, Pu, and He Prefectures into rebellion; Wang Jian sent campaign army-and-horse commissioner Wang Zong'an leading thirty thousand troops to join Dongchuan and Wuxin forces in suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Du Congfa incited rebellion in Chang, Pu, and He Prefectures with false prophecies; Wang Jian sent campaign commissioner Wang Zong'an with thirty thousand men, joined by Dongchuan and Wuxin troops, to crush them.

sentences.zh: 宗黯，即吉諫也。

translations.literal: Zong'an was in fact Ji Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'an was the same man as Ji Jian.

sentences.zh: 崔胤請上盡誅宦官，但以宮人掌內諸司事。

translations.literal: Cui Yin asked the emperor to execute all the eunuchs and let only palace women manage the inner bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin urged the emperor to execute every eunuch and put palace women in charge of the inner offices.

sentences.zh: 宦官屬耳，頗聞之，韓全誨等涕泣求哀於上，上乃令胤：「有事封疏以聞，勿口奏。」

translations.literal: The eunuchs had sharp ears and heard much of it; Han Quanhui and others wept and begged mercy from the emperor. The emperor then ordered Yin: "When there is business, submit sealed memorials—do not report orally."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs overheard. Han Quanhui and the rest wept and begged the emperor for mercy. The emperor then told Yin: "Put your proposals in writing—no more oral reports to the throne."

sentences.zh: 宦官求美女知書者數人，內之宮中，陰令詗察其事，盡得胤密謀，上不之覺也。

translations.literal: The eunuchs sought several beautiful, literate women and brought them into the palace, secretly ordering them to investigate the matter; they learned all of Yin's secret plots, and the emperor did not realize it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs recruited literate palace women and planted them to spy on Yin. They learned his entire plot, and the emperor never knew.

sentences.zh: 全誨等大懼，每宴聚，流涕相訣別，日夜謀所以去胤之術。

translations.literal: Quanhui and the others were greatly afraid; at every feast they wept and took leave of one another, day and night plotting means to remove Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui and his allies were terrified. At every gathering they wept as if saying farewell, plotting day and night how to destroy Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤時領三司使，全誨等教禁軍對上喧噪，訴胤減損冬衣。

translations.literal: Yin then held the post of commissioner of the Three Bureaus; Quanhui and the others instructed the palace guard to clamor before the emperor, complaining that Yin had cut their winter clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yin still controlled the Three Bureaus. Quanhui's faction stirred up the palace guard to shout before the throne that Yin had shorted their winter uniforms.

sentences.zh: 上不得已，解胤鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice and removed Yin from the Salt and Iron Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice but to strip Yin of the Salt and Iron Commission.

sentences.zh: 時朱全忠、李茂貞各有挾天子令諸侯之意，全忠欲上幸東都，茂貞欲上幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: At the time Zhu Quanzhong and Li Maozhen each had the intent of holding the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords; Quanzhong wished the emperor to visit the Eastern Capital, Maozhen wished him to visit Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong and Li Maozhen each wanted to hold the emperor hostage to command the regional lords—Quanzhong wanted him in the Eastern Capital, Maozhen in Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 胤知謀洩，事急，遺朱全忠書，稱被密詔，令全忠以兵迎車駕，且言：「昨者返正，皆令公良圖，而鳳翔先入朝抄取其功。

translations.literal: Yin knew the plot had leaked and matters were urgent; he sent a letter to Zhu Quanzhong, claiming a secret edict ordering Quanzhong to bring troops to welcome the imperial carriage, and saying: "When the restoration happened yesterday, all was for you to plan well—but Fengxiang entered court first and seized the credit.
translations.idiomatic: Yin learned the plot was exposed and wrote urgently to Zhu Quanzhong, claiming a secret edict to bring troops and escort the emperor. "You engineered the restoration," he wrote, "but Fengxiang got to court first and stole the credit.

sentences.zh: 今不速來，必成罪人，豈惟功為他人所有，且見征討矣！」

translations.literal: If you do not come quickly now, you will surely become a criminal—not only will the merit belong to others, but you will also face punitive expedition!"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not come at once, you will be treated as a criminal—not only will the glory go to someone else, but you will face attack!"

sentences.zh: 全忠得書，秋，七月，甲寅，遽歸大梁發兵。

translations.literal: Quanzhong received the letter; in autumn, the seventh month, on jiayin, he hurriedly returned to Daliang and mobilized troops.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong received the letter. In autumn, the seventh month, on jiayin, he raced back to Daliang and mobilized his army.

sentences.zh: 西川龍台鎮使王宗侃等討杜從法，平之。

translations.literal: Wang Zongkan, commissioner of Longtai Town in Xichuan, and others suppressed Du Congfa and pacified the region.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongkan of Xichuan's Longtai command and others suppressed Du Congfa and restored order.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲申，上問韓偓曰：「聞陸扆不樂吾返正，正旦易服，乘小馬出啟夏門，有諸？」

translations.literal: Eighth month, on jiashen, the emperor asked Han Wo: "I hear Lu Yi was displeased at my restoration—on New Year's Day he changed clothes, mounted a small horse, and went out the Qixia Gate—is this so?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiashen, the emperor asked Han Wo: "I hear Lu Yi was unhappy about my restoration—on New Year's Day he changed clothes, mounted a pony, and slipped out the Qixia Gate. Is that true?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「返正之謀，獨臣與崔胤輩數人知之，扆不知也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Of the plot for restoration, only I and a few like Cui Yin knew—Yi did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Wo replied: "Only a handful of us, including Cui Yin and myself, knew about the restoration plot. Yi was not among them.

sentences.zh: 一旦忽聞宮中有變，人情能不驚駭！

translations.literal: Suddenly one day hearing that the palace had changed—how could human hearts not be startled and terrified!
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly hearing the palace had been seized—who would not panic?

sentences.zh: 易服逃避，何妨有之！

translations.literal: Changing clothes to flee—what harm if it happened!
translations.idiomatic: Changing clothes to flee would be only natural!

sentences.zh: 陛下責其為宰相無死難之志則可也，至於不樂返正，恐出於讒人之口，願陛下察之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty may blame him as a chancellor for lacking the will to die in the crisis—that is acceptable; but as for displeasure at the restoration, I fear that comes from slanderers' mouths—I beg Your Majesty to examine it."
translations.idiomatic: You may blame him as a chancellor for lacking the courage to die for the throne—that is fair. But the claim that he opposed your restoration likely comes from slanderers. Please look into it."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 韓全誨等懼誅，謀以兵制上，乃與李繼昭、李繼誨、李彥弼、李繼筠深相結，繼昭獨不肯從。

translations.literal: Han Quanhui and the others, fearing execution, plotted to control the emperor by force; they formed deep ties with Li Jizhao, Li Jihui, Li Yanbi, and Li Jiyun—only Jizhao refused to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanhui and his faction, fearing death, plotted to control the emperor by force. They enlisted Li Jizhao, Li Jihui, Li Yanbi, and Li Jiyun—only Jizhao refused.

sentences.zh: 它日，上問韓偓：「外間何所聞？」

translations.literal: Another day the emperor asked Han Wo: "What is heard outside?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor asked Han Wo: "What are people saying outside?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「惟聞敕使憂懼，與功臣及繼筠交結，將致不安，亦未知其果然不耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I have only heard that the edict commissioners are fearful and anxious, forming ties with meritorious officials and Jiyun, which will bring unrest—I do not yet know whether it is truly so."
translations.idiomatic: Wo replied: "I hear only that the edict commissioners are frightened and allying with the meritorious officers and Jiyun—trouble may be coming, though I cannot yet be sure."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「是不虛矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That is not untrue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is no rumor.

sentences.zh: 比日繼誨、彥弼輩語漸倔強，令人難耐。

translations.literal: In recent days Jihui, Yanbi, and the rest have grown increasingly defiant in speech—it is hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: Lately Jihui, Yanbi, and the rest have grown brazen and insufferable.

sentences.zh: 令狐渙欲令朕召崔胤及全誨等於內殿，置酒和解之，何如？」

translations.literal: Linghu Huan wishes to have me summon Cui Yin and Quanhui and the rest to the inner hall, set out wine, and reconcile them—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Huan wants me to summon Cui Yin and Quanhui to the inner hall for a banquet and patch things up. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「如此則彼凶悖益甚。」

translations.literal: He replied: "If so, their violence and insolence will grow all the worse."
translations.idiomatic: Wo replied: "That would only make them bolder and more dangerous."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「為之奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What is to be done about it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Then what should I do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「獨有顯罪數人，速加竄逐，餘者許其自新，庶幾可息。

translations.literal: He replied: "Only by openly convicting several men and quickly banishing them, allowing the rest to reform themselves, might it perhaps be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Wo said: "Punish the ringleaders openly and banish them quickly. Let the rest reform themselves—that may calm things.

sentences.zh: 若一無所問，彼必知陛下心有所貯，益不自安，事終未了耳。」

translations.literal: If nothing at all is asked, they will surely know the emperor's heart harbors resentment, grow even less secure, and the matter will never end."
translations.idiomatic: If you punish no one, they will know you still bear a grudge and grow more restless—the crisis will never end."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Good advice!"

sentences.zh: 既而宦官自恃黨援已成，稍不遵敕旨；

translations.literal: Before long the eunuchs, relying on their factional support as already formed, gradually ceased to obey edicts;
translations.idiomatic: Before long the eunuchs, confident their faction was secure, began ignoring imperial orders;

sentences.zh: 上或出之使監軍，或黜守諸陵，皆不行，上無如之何。

translations.literal: when the emperor would send them out as army supervisors or demote them to guard the imperial tombs, none would go—the emperor could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor tried to post them as army supervisors or banish them to guard the imperial tombs, they simply refused—and he was powerless to stop them.

sentences.zh: 或告楊行密雲，錢鏐為盜所殺。

translations.literal: Someone reported to Yang Xingmi that Qian Liu had been killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached Yang Xingmi that Qian Liu had been killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 行密遣步軍都指揮使李神福等將兵取杭州，兩浙將顧全武等列八寨以拒之。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent infantry commander Li Shenfu and others leading troops to take Hangzhou; Liang-Zhe generals Gu Quanwu and others set up eight camps to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent infantry commander Li Shenfu to seize Hangzhou; Gu Quanwu and other Liang-Zhe generals threw up eight camps to block him.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸丑，上急召韓偓，謂曰：「聞全忠欲來除君側之惡，大是盡忠，然須令與茂貞共其功。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on guichou, the emperor urgently summoned Han Wo and said: "I hear Quanzhong wishes to come and remove the evil at the ruler's side—great loyalty indeed—but he must be made to share the merit with Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guichou, the emperor urgently summoned Han Wo. "I hear Quanzhong is coming to purge the evil at my side—that shows loyalty," he said, "but he must share the credit with Maozhen.

sentences.zh: 若兩帥交爭，則事危矣。

translations.literal: If the two commanders contend with each other, the affair will be perilous.
translations.idiomatic: If those two warlords clash, the throne itself is in danger.

sentences.zh: 卿為我語崔胤，速飛書兩鎮，使相與合謀，則善矣。

translations.literal: You speak for me to Cui Yin—quickly send flying letters to the two commands, so they may plot together; that would be well.
translations.idiomatic: Tell Cui Yin to send urgent messages to both commands and get them to cooperate—that would be best.

sentences.zh: ?比尚絎上又謂偓曰：「繼誨、彥弼輩驕橫益甚，累日前與繼筠同入，輒於殿東令小兒歌以侑酒，令人驚駭。」

translations.literal: [Text corrupt] the emperor also said to Wo: "Jihui, Yanbi, and the rest grow ever more arrogant and overbearing; several days ago they entered with Jiyun and had children sing east of the hall to accompany the wine—it was shocking."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also told Wo: "Jihui, Yanbi, and the rest grow bolder by the day. A few days ago they came in with Jiyun and had boys sing east of the hall to entertain them over wine—it was outrageous."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣必知其然，茲事失之於初。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject was sure it would come to this—the fault lay at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Wo replied: "I knew it would come to this. The mistake was made at the start.

sentences.zh: 當正旦立功之時，但應以官爵、田宅、金帛酬之，不應聽其恣出入禁中。

translations.literal: At the time of the New Year's Day achievement, they should only have been rewarded with offices, ranks, estates, and gold and silk—not permitted to come and go freely within the Forbidden Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When they restored you on New Year's Day, they should have been paid off with titles, estates, and gold—not given free run of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 此輩素無知識，數求入對，或妄論朝政，或僭易薦人，稍有不從，則生怨望。

translations.literal: These people by nature lack understanding; they repeatedly ask for audience, sometimes recklessly discuss court politics, sometimes presumptuously recommend people for office—if the slightest thing is not granted, resentment arises.
translations.idiomatic: These men know nothing of propriety. They demand audiences, meddle in policy, push their own nominees—and resent the slightest refusal.

sentences.zh: 況惟知嗜利，為敕使以厚利雇之，令其如此耳。

translations.literal: Moreover they know only greed for profit—the edict commissioners hire them with rich rewards and make them act thus.
translations.idiomatic: And they care only for profit—the edict commissioners pay them well to behave this way.

sentences.zh: 崔胤本留衛兵，欲以制敕使也，今敕使、衛兵相與為一，將若之何！

translations.literal: Cui Yin originally kept guard troops to control the edict commissioners—now edict commissioners and guard troops have become one; what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin posted guard troops to control the edict commissioners—but now commissioners and guards are one faction. What can be done!

sentences.zh: 汴兵若來，必與岐兵斗於闕下，臣竊寒心。」

translations.literal: If Bian troops come, they will surely fight Qi troops beneath the palace gates—Your subject secretly shudders at the heart."
translations.idiomatic: If Bian troops arrive, they will fight Qi troops at the palace gates—I tremble at the thought."

sentences.zh: 上但愀然憂沮而已。

translations.literal: The emperor could only look grim and sink in worry and dejection.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could only sit there, grim and helpless.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊戌，朱全忠大舉兵發大梁。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on wuxu, Zhu Quanzhong mobilized a great army and set out from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuxu, Zhu Quanzhong marched from Daliang at the head of a massive army.

sentences.zh: 李神福與顧全武相拒久之，神福?窈擠蘗使出入臥內。

translations.literal: Li Shenfu and Gu Quanwu faced each other for a long time; Shenfu [text corrupt] had attendants come in and out of his inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu and Gu Quanwu had faced off for a long time. Shenfu took Hangzhou captives and had them come and go from his inner quarters—as if at ease.

sentences.zh: 神福謂諸將曰：「杭兵尚強，我師且當夜還。」

translations.literal: Shenfu said to the generals: "The Hangzhou troops are still strong—our army should withdraw by night."
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu told his officers: "Hangzhou's army is still strong. We should pull out tonight."

sentences.zh: 杭俘走告全武，神福命勿追，暮遣羸兵先行，神福為殿，使行營都尉呂師造伏兵青山下。

translations.literal: A Hangzhou captive ran to tell Quanwu; Shenfu ordered that he not be pursued. At dusk he sent weak troops ahead first, Shenfu brought up the rear, and had campaign commander Lu Shizao lie in ambush below Qing Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: A Hangzhou prisoner escaped and warned Quanwu. Shenfu ordered no pursuit. At dusk he sent his weakest troops ahead while he brought up the rear, with Lu Shizao ambushing below Qing Mountain.

sentences.zh: 全武素輕神福，出兵追之。

translations.literal: Quanwu had always looked down on Shenfu and led troops out in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Quanwu had always despised Shenfu and marched out in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 神福、師造夾擊，大破之，斬首五千級，生擒全武。

translations.literal: Shenfu and Shizao struck from both sides, routed them utterly, claimed five thousand heads, and captured Quanwu alive.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu and Shizao attacked from both flanks and crushed the pursuit force, claiming five thousand heads and taking Quanwu alive.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐聞之，驚泣曰：「喪我良將！」

translations.literal: Qian Liu heard of it and cried out in shock: "I have lost my fine general!"
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Liu heard, he wept in shock: "I've lost my best general!"

sentences.zh: 神福進攻臨安，兩浙將秦昶帥眾三千降之。

translations.literal: Shenfu advanced to attack Lin'an; Liang-Zhe general Qin Chang leading three thousand men surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu pressed on to Lin'an; Qin Chang of Liang-Zhe surrendered with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 韓全誨聞朱全忠將至，丁酉，令李繼誨、李彥弼等勒兵劫上，請幸鳳翔，宮禁諸門皆增兵防守，人及文書出入搜閱甚嚴。

translations.literal: Han Quanhui, hearing Zhu Quanzhong was about to arrive, on dingyou ordered Li Jihui, Li Yanbi, and others to seize troops and coerce the emperor, requesting that he visit Fengxiang; at every gate of the palace precincts additional troops were posted on guard, and people and documents passing in and out were searched with great strictness.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Zhu Quanzhong was coming, Han Quanhui on dingyou had Li Jihui, Li Yanbi, and others seize the emperor at swordpoint and demand he go to Fengxiang. Every palace gate was reinforced, and people and documents were searched on entry and exit.

sentences.zh: 上遣人密賜崔胤御札，言皆淒愴，末云：「我為宗社大計，勢須西行，卿等但東行也。

translations.literal: The emperor sent someone to secretly bestow on Cui Yin an imperial letter; every word was mournful, ending: "For the great plan of the altars of state I must go west—you need only go east.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent Cui Yin an imperial letter, every line full of grief. It ended: "For the dynasty's sake I must go west. You should go east.

sentences.zh: 惆悵！

translations.literal: Melancholy!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 惆悵！」

translations.literal: Melancholy!"
translations.idiomatic: Alas!"

sentences.zh: 戊戌，上遣趙國夫人出語韓偓：「朝來彥弼輩無禮極甚，欲召卿對，其勢未可。」

translations.literal: On wuxu, the emperor sent the Lady of Zhao out to speak to Han Wo: "This morning Yanbi and the rest were utterly without propriety; I wished to summon you for audience, but the situation will not allow it."
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the emperor sent the Lady of Zhao to tell Han Wo: "Yanbi and his friends were insufferably rude this morning. I wanted to summon you, but it is not safe."

sentences.zh: 且言：「上與皇后但涕泣相同。」

translations.literal: She also said: "The emperor and the empress can only weep together."
translations.idiomatic: She added: "The emperor and empress do nothing but weep together."

sentences.zh: 自是，學士不復得對矣。

translations.literal: From then on the academicians were no longer granted audience.
translations.idiomatic: After that, Hanlin academicians were never again admitted to audience.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，全誨等令上入閣召百官，迫寢正月丙午敕書，悉如咸通以來近例。

translations.literal: On guimao, Quanhui and the others had the emperor enter the pavilion to summon the hundred officials, forcing the suspension of the bingwu edict of the first month and restoring everything to recent precedent since Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Quanhui forced the emperor into the pavilion to summon officials and set aside the bingwu edict from the first month, restoring eunuch power to what it had been since the Xiantong era.

sentences.zh: 是日，開延英，全誨等即侍側，同議政事。

translations.literal: That day the Yanying Hall was opened; Quanhui and the others immediately attended at his side and jointly deliberated on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Yanying Hall opened for business—with Quanhui and his allies at the emperor's side, jointly deciding policy.

sentences.zh: 丁未，神策都指揮使李繼筠遣部兵掠內庫寶貨、帷帳、法物，韓全誨遣人密送諸王、宮人先之鳳翔。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Shence commander Li Jiyun dispatched his troops to plunder the inner treasury's treasures, curtains, and ritual objects; Han Quanhui sent men to secretly escort the princes and palace women ahead to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Li Jiyun looted the inner treasury of treasures, hangings, and ritual objects while Quanhui secretly sent the princes and palace women ahead to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 戊申，朱全忠至河中，表請車駕幸東都，京城大駭，士民亡竄山谷。

translations.literal: On wushen, Zhu Quanzhong reached Hezhong and memorialized requesting the imperial carriage visit the Eastern Capital; the capital was greatly terrified, and officials and commoners fled and hid in the mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Zhu Quanzhong reached Hezhong and petitioned for the emperor to come to the Eastern Capital. Panic swept the capital as officials and commoners fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 是日，百官皆不入朝，闕前寂無人。

translations.literal: That day none of the hundred officials entered court; before the palace gates there was silence and no one.
translations.idiomatic: That day no official came to court—the palace gates stood empty and silent.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己酉朔，李繼筠等勒兵闕下，禁人出入，諸軍大掠。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, first day jiyou, Li Jiyun and others deployed troops beneath the palace gates, forbidding people to enter or leave; the various armies looted on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day, Li Jiyun posted troops at the palace gates and sealed the city while the armies plundered at will.

sentences.zh: 士民衣紙及布襦者，滿街極目。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners wearing paper and cloth tunics filled the streets as far as the eye could see.
translations.idiomatic: The streets were full of people clad in paper and coarse cloth—the looters had stripped them bare.

sentences.zh: 韓建以幕僚司馬鄴知匡國留後。

translations.literal: Han Jian appointed his staff member Sima Ye acting commissioner of Kuangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian made staff officer Sima Ye acting commissioner of Kuangguo.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠引四鎮兵七萬趣同州，鄴迎降。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong led seventy thousand troops of the four commands toward Tong Prefecture; Ye came out to welcome and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong marched seventy thousand men from his four commands toward Tong Prefecture; Ye surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 韓全誨等以李繼昭不與之同，遏絕不令見上。

translations.literal: Han Quanhui and the others, because Li Jizhao would not join them, blocked and cut off access and would not let him see the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Jizhao refused to join them, Quanhui's faction cut him off from the emperor entirely.

sentences.zh: 時崔胤居第在開化坊，繼昭帥所部六十餘人及關東諸道兵在京師者共守衛之。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Yin's residence was in Kaihua Ward; Jizhao led his more than sixty followers and troops of the Guandong circuits then in the capital to guard it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin lived in Kaihua Ward. Jizhao posted his sixty-odd men plus Guandong troops stationed in the capital to guard the residence.

sentences.zh: 百官及士民避亂者，皆往依之。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners fleeing the disorder all went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and civilians fleeing the chaos all took refuge there.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，上遣供奉官張紹孫召百官，崔胤等皆表辭不至。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the emperor sent tribute officer Zhang Shaosun to summon the hundred officials; Cui Yin and the rest all submitted memorials declining and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the emperor sent Zhang Shaosun to summon the officials. Cui Yin and the others all sent excuses and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 壬子，韓全誨等陳兵殿前，言於上曰：「全忠以大兵逼京師，欲劫天子幸洛陽，求傳禪。

translations.literal: On renzi, Han Quanhui and the others arrayed troops before the hall and said to the emperor: "Quanzhong with a great army presses on the capital, wishing to seize the Son of Heaven and take him to Luoyang and seek the transfer of the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Quanhui arrayed troops before the throne and told the emperor: "Quanzhong is marching on the capital with a huge army. He means to seize you, take you to Luoyang, and force your abdication.

sentences.zh: 臣等請奉陛下幸鳳翔，收兵拒之。

translations.literal: We your subjects beg to escort Your Majesty to Fengxiang, gather troops, and resist him.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to come with us to Fengxiang, where we can gather troops and resist him.

sentences.zh: 「上不許，杖劍登乞巧樓。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent; grasping his sword he ascended the Qiqiao Tower.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused. Sword in hand, he climbed the Qiqiao Tower.

sentences.zh: 全誨等逼上下樓，上行才及壽春殿，李彥弼已於御院縱火。

translations.literal: Quanhui and the others forced him up and down from the tower; the emperor had only reached the Shouchun Hall when Li Yanbi had already set fire in the imperial courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui's men forced him down. He had barely reached the Shouchun Hall when Yanbi set fire to the imperial courtyard.

sentences.zh: 是日冬至，上獨坐思政殿，翹一足，一足蹋欄干，庭無群臣，旁無侍者。

translations.literal: That day was the winter solstice; the emperor sat alone in the Sizheng Hall, one foot raised, one foot on the railing—no hundred officials in the courtyard, no attendants at his side.
translations.idiomatic: It was the winter solstice. The emperor sat alone in the Sizheng Hall, one foot on the rail, the courtyard empty of officials, no attendants at his side.

sentences.zh: 頃之，不得已，與皇后、妃嬪、諸王百餘人皆上馬，慟哭聲不絕，出門，回顧禁中，火已赫然。

translations.literal: Before long, having no choice, together with the empress, consorts, and more than a hundred princes he all mounted horses; wailing never ceased. Going out the gate and looking back at the Forbidden Palace, the fire was already blazing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with no choice left, he mounted with the empress, consorts, and more than a hundred princes, weeping all the way. At the gate he looked back—the palace was already in flames.

sentences.zh: 是夕，宿鄠縣。

translations.literal: That evening they lodged at E County.
translations.idiomatic: That night they stopped at E County.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣司馬鄴入華州，謂韓建曰：「公不早知過自歸，又煩此軍少留城下矣。」

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent Sima Ye into Hua Prefecture and said to Han Jian: "If you had not known your fault early and surrendered of yourself, this army would not have had to linger beneath your walls."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Sima Ye to Han Jian at Hua Prefecture: "If you had surrendered sooner, my army would not have had to camp at your gates."

sentences.zh: 是日，全忠自故市引兵南渡渭，韓建遣節度副使李巨川請降，獻銀三萬兩助軍，全忠乃西南趣赤水。

translations.literal: That day Quanzhong led troops from Gushi south across the Wei; Han Jian sent deputy commissioner Li Juchuan to request surrender, presenting thirty thousand taels of silver to aid the army, and Quanzhong then pressed southwest toward Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: That day Quanzhong crossed the Wei south of Gushi. Han Jian sent Li Juchuan to surrender with thirty thousand taels of silver for the army, and Quanzhong marched southwest toward Chishui.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，李茂貞迎車駕於田家磑，上下馬慰接之。

translations.literal: On guichou, Li Maozhen welcomed the imperial carriage at Tianjia Mill, dismounting to comfort and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Li Maozhen met the imperial procession at Tianjia Mill, dismounting to greet the emperor with words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，車駕至盩厔；

translations.literal: On jiayin, the imperial carriage reached Zhouzhi;
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the procession reached Zhouzhi;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，留一日。

translations.literal: On yimao, they remained one day.
translations.idiomatic: on yimao they rested a day.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠至零口西，聞車駕西幸，與僚佐議，復引兵還赤水。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong reached west of Lingkou, heard the imperial carriage had gone west on tour, consulted with his staff, and again led troops back to Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong reached west of Lingkou. Learning the emperor had fled west, he consulted his staff and turned back toward Chishui.

sentences.zh: 左僕射至仕張濬說全忠曰：「韓建，茂貞之黨，不先取之，必為後患。

translations.literal: Retired Left Vice Director Zhang Jun urged Quanzhong, saying: "Han Jian is a partisan of Maozhen—if he is not taken first, he will surely become a later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The retired Left Vice Director Zhang Jun urged Quanzhong: "Han Jian is Maozhen's ally. Take him now or he will trouble you later.

sentences.zh: ?比□椅漚擫斜砣疤熳有曳鏘瓔乃引兵逼其城。

translations.literal: [Text corrupt] thereupon led troops to press on the city.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then led his army straight to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 建單騎迎謁，全忠責之，對曰：「建目不知書，凡表章書檄，皆李巨川所為。」

translations.literal: Jian came out alone on horseback to welcome and pay respects; Quanzhong rebuked him. He replied: "Jian's eyes do not know writing—all memorials, letters, and proclamations were done by Li Juchuan."
translations.idiomatic: Jian rode out alone to greet him. Quanzhong rebuked him. Jian replied: "I cannot read or write—Li Juchuan drafted every document in my name."

sentences.zh: 全忠以巨川常為建畫策，斬之軍門。

translations.literal: Quanzhong, because Juchuan had often plotted strategy for Jian, beheaded him at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong had Juchuan beheaded at the army gate for drafting Jian's policies.

sentences.zh: 謂建曰：「公許人，可即往衣錦。」

translations.literal: He said to Jian: "You gave your word—you may go at once to return in brocade."
translations.idiomatic: He told Jian: "You gave your word. Go home in glory."

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以建為忠武節度使，理陳州，以兵援送之；

translations.literal: On dingsi, Jian was made military commissioner of Zhongwu, administering Chen Prefecture, and escorted there with troops;
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Jian was made military commissioner of Zhongwu at Chen Prefecture and escorted there under guard;

sentences.zh: 以前商州刺史李存權知華州，徙忠武節度使趙珝為匡國節度使。

translations.literal: former Shang Prefecture governor Li Cunquan was made acting governor of Hua Prefecture, and former Zhongwu military commissioner Zhao Xu was transferred to military commissioner of Kuangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunquan, former governor of Shang Prefecture, took Hua Prefecture, and Zhao Xu was moved from Zhongwu to Kuangguo.

sentences.zh: 車駕之在華州也，商賈輻湊，韓建重征之，二年，得錢九百萬緡。

translations.literal: While the imperial carriage was at Hua Prefecture, merchants gathered in crowds; Han Jian heavily taxed them and in two years obtained nine million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Hua Prefecture, merchants flocked there. Han Jian taxed them heavily and in two years amassed nine million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 至是，全忠盡取之。

translations.literal: At this time Quanzhong took it all.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong seized every coin of it.

sentences.zh: 是時京師無天子，行在無宰相，崔胤使太子太師盧渥等二百餘人列狀請朱全忠西迎車駕，又使王溥至赤水見全忠計事。

translations.literal: At this time the capital had no Son of Heaven and the traveling court had no chancellor; Cui Yin had Crown Prince Grand Preceptor Lu Wo and more than two hundred others submit a joint petition asking Zhu Quanzhong to welcome the imperial carriage from the west, and also sent Wang Pu to Chishui to see Quanzhong and plan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had no emperor and the traveling court no chancellor. Cui Yin had Lu Wo and more than two hundred officials petition Quanzhong to escort the emperor back, and sent Wang Pu to Chishui to confer with him.

sentences.zh: 全忠復書曰：「進則懼脅君之謗，退則懷負國之慚，然不敢不勉。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong replied in a letter: "Advance and I fear the slander of coercing the ruler; retreat and I bear the shame of betraying the state—yet I dare not fail to strive."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong wrote back: "If I advance, I will be accused of coercing the throne; if I hold back, I will be shamed as a traitor. Still, I dare not fail to act."

sentences.zh: 戊午，全忠發赤水。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Quanzhong set out from Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Quanzhong marched out from Chishui.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以兵部侍郎盧光啟權句當中書事。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Vice Minister of War Lu Guangqi was made acting director of Chancellery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Lu Guangqi, Vice Minister of War, was put in charge of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 車駕留岐山三日，壬戌，至鳳翔。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage remained at Qishan three days; on renxu it reached Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The procession rested three days at Qishan, then on renxu reached Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠至長安，宰相帥百官班迎於長樂坡。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong reached Chang'an; the chancellors led the hundred officials in formal welcome at Changle Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong reached Chang'an, where the chancellors led the officials in formal welcome at Changle Slope.

sentences.zh: 明日行，復班辭於臨皋驛。

translations.literal: The next day as he departed, they again formed ranks to take leave at Lingao Post.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, as he departed, they formed ranks again to bid farewell at Lingao Post.

sentences.zh: 全忠賞李繼昭之功，初令權知匡國留後，復留為兩街制置使，賜與甚厚，繼昭盡獻其兵八千人。

translations.literal: Quanzhong rewarded Li Jizhao's merit, first appointing him acting commissioner of Kuangguo, then retaining him as commissioner for the Two Streets, with lavish gifts; Jizhao surrendered all his eight thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong rewarded Jizhao, first making him acting commissioner of Kuangguo, then keeping him as commissioner for the Two Streets with lavish gifts. Jizhao turned over all eight thousand of his men.

sentences.zh: 全忠使判官李擇、裴鑄入奏事，稱：「奉密詔及得崔胤書，令臣將兵入朝。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent judge-advocates Li Ze and Pei Zhu to enter and report affairs, stating: "Obeying a secret edict and receiving Cui Yin's letter, I was ordered to bring troops to court."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Li Ze and Pei Zhu to report to the throne: "By secret edict and Cui Yin's letter, I was ordered to bring troops to court."

sentences.zh: 韓全誨等矯詔答以：「朕避災至此，非宦官所劫，密詔皆崔胤詐為之，卿宜斂兵歸保土宇。」

translations.literal: Han Quanhui and the others forged an edict in reply: "We came here to escape calamity—it was not eunuchs who seized us. The secret edicts were all fraudulently made by Cui Yin. You should withdraw your troops and return to guard your own territory."
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui forged a reply: "We came here to escape disaster—not because eunuchs seized us. Yin's secret edicts are forgeries. Withdraw your troops and go home."

sentences.zh: 茂貞遣其將符道昭屯武功以拒全忠，癸亥，全忠將康懷貞擊破之。

translations.literal: Maozhen sent his general Fu Daozhao to camp at Wugong to resist Quanzhong; on guihai, Quanzhong's general Kang Huaizhen defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen posted Fu Daozhao at Wugong to block Quanzhong. On guihai Kang Huaizhen routed him.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以盧光啟為右諫議大夫，參知機務。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Lu Guangqi was made Right Remonstrance Censor and participant in confidential state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Lu Guangqi was made Right Remonstrance Censor and given a voice in confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，朱全忠至鳳翔，軍於城東。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Zhu Quanzhong reached Fengxiang and encamped east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Zhu Quanzhong reached Fengxiang and encamped east of the walls.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞登城謂曰：「天子避災，非臣下無禮，讒人誤公至此。」

translations.literal: Li Maozhen mounted the wall and said: "The Son of Heaven came to escape calamity—it is not that subjects were without propriety; slanderers misled Your Lordship to this point."
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen mounted the wall and called out: "The emperor came here to escape disaster. My men were not disrespectful—slanderers misled you."

sentences.zh: 全忠報曰：「韓全誨劫遷天子，今來問罪，迎扈還宮。

translations.literal: Quanzhong replied: "Han Quanhui seized and moved the Son of Heaven—I come now to demand accountability and escort him back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong replied: "Han Quanhui kidnapped the emperor. I have come to punish him and escort the throne home.

sentences.zh: 岐王苟不預謀，何煩陳諭！」

translations.literal: If Prince of Qi was not party to the plot, why trouble yourself with explanations!"
translations.idiomatic: If you had no part in this, why bother explaining yourself!"

sentences.zh: 上屢詔全忠還鎮，全忠乃拜表奉辭。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly issued an edict Quanzhong to return to his command; Quanzhong then submitted a memorial in formal leave-taking.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly ordered Quanzhong back to his post. Quanzhong submitted a formal farewell memorial.

sentences.zh: 辛未，移兵北趣邠州。

translations.literal: On xinwei, he moved his army north toward Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he marched north toward Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，制：守司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事崔胤責授工部尚書，戶部侍郎、同平章事裴樞罷守本官。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, an edict: acting Minister of Works and concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor Cui Yin was demoted to Minister of Works; Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Councilor Pei Shu was removed and kept his original office.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu an edict demoted Cui Yin from Grand Councilor to Minister of Works and stripped Pei Shu of the Grand Councilor title, leaving him Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，朱全忠攻邠州。

translations.literal: On yihai, Zhu Quanzhong attacked Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Zhu Quanzhong attacked Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，靜難節度使李繼徽請降，復姓名楊崇本。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Jingnan military commissioner Li Jihui requested surrender and had his original name Yang Chongben restored.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Jingnan commissioner Li Jihui surrendered and had his original name Yang Chongben restored.

sentences.zh: 全忠質其妻於河中，令崇本仍鎮邠州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong held his wife hostage at Hezhong and ordered Chongben to continue governing Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong kept Chongben's wife hostage at Hezhong and let him remain at Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 全忠之西入關也，韓全誨、李茂貞以詔命徵兵河東，茂貞仍以書求援於李克用。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong entered the passes to the west, Han Quanhui and Li Maozhen by edict summoned troops from Hedong; Maozhen also sent a letter requesting aid from Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong entered the passes, Quanhui and Maozhen issued edicts summoning Hedong troops, and Maozhen wrote Li Keyong begging for help.

sentences.zh: 克用遣李嗣昭將五千騎自沁州趣晉州，與汴兵戰於平陽北，破之。

translations.literal: Keyong sent Li Sizhao leading five thousand cavalry from Qin Prefecture toward Jin Prefecture; they fought Bian troops north of Pingyang and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Li Sizhao with five thousand cavalry from Qin Prefecture toward Jin Prefecture and routed Bian forces north of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，全忠發邠州。

translations.literal: On yihai, Quanzhong set out from Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Quanzhong marched out from Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，次三原。

translations.literal: On wuyin, he halted at Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he halted at Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸未，崔胤至三原見全忠，趣之迎駕。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on guiwei, Cui Yin reached Sanyuan, saw Quanzhong, and urged him to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guiwei, Cui Yin met Quanzhong at Sanyuan and pressed him to escort the emperor back.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，全忠遣朱友寧攻盩厔，不下。

translations.literal: On yichou, Quanzhong sent Zhu Youning to attack Zhouzhi; it was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Quanzhong sent Zhu Youning against Zhouzhi, but the city held.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，全忠自往督戰，盩厔降，屠之。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Quanzhong went in person to direct the battle; Zhouzhi surrendered and was put to the sword.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Quanzhong personally directed the assault. Zhouzhi surrendered and was slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 全忠令崔胤帥百官及京城居民悉遷於華州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong ordered Cui Yin to lead the hundred officials and all residents of the capital to relocate to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong ordered Cui Yin to move all officials and capital residents to Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔以裴贄充大明宮留守。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Pei Zan custodian of the Daming Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zan was appointed custodian of the Daming Palace.

sentences.zh: 清海節度使徐彥若薨，遺表薦行軍司馬劉隱權留後。

translations.literal: Qinghai military commissioner Xu Yanruo died; in his final memorial he recommended campaign secretary Liu Yin as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanruo, military commissioner of Qinghai, died and recommended campaign secretary Liu Yin as acting commissioner in his final memorial.

sentences.zh: 李神福知錢鏐定不死，而臨安城堅，久攻不拔，欲歸，恐為鏐所邀，乃遣人守衛鏐祖考丘壟，禁樵采，又使顧全武通家信。

translations.literal: Li Shenfu knew Qian Liu was certainly not dead, and that Lin'an's walls were strong and long besieged without capture; wishing to return, he feared Liu would intercept him. He therefore sent men to guard the tombs of Liu's ancestors, forbade cutting wood and gathering, and also had Gu Quanwu exchange letters with his family.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu learned Qian Liu was alive and that Lin'an's walls were too strong to take. Wanting to withdraw but fearing ambush, he posted guards at the Qian family tombs, forbade woodcutting nearby, and let Gu Quanwu write home.

sentences.zh: 鏐遣使謝之。

translations.literal: Liu sent envoys to thank him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent envoys to thank him.

sentences.zh: 神福於要路多張旗幟為虛寨，鏐以為淮南兵大至，遂請和。

translations.literal: Shenfu at key roads raised many banners and flags as dummy camps; Liu thought Huainan troops had arrived in great force and thereupon requested peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu planted dummy camps with banners along the main roads. Qian Liu thought a massive Huainan army had arrived and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 神福受其犒賂而還。

translations.literal: Shenfu accepted his gifts of reward and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu took the tribute offered and marched home.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠之入關也，戎昭節度使馮行襲遣副使魯崇矩聽命於全忠。

translations.literal: When Zhu Quanzhong entered the passes, Rongzhao military commissioner Feng Xingxi sent deputy commissioner Lu Chongju to obey Quanzhong's orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong entered the passes, Rongzhao commissioner Feng Xingxi sent Lu Chongju to place himself under Quanzhong's command.

sentences.zh: 韓全誨遣中使二十餘人分道征江、淮兵屯金州，以脅全忠，行襲盡殺中使，收其詔敕送全忠。

translations.literal: Han Quanhui sent more than twenty palace commissioners by separate routes to summon Jiang-Huai troops to camp at Jin Prefecture to coerce Quanzhong; Xingxi killed all the commissioners, seized their edicts and orders, and sent them to Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui sent more than twenty palace commissioners to summon Jiang-Huai troops to Jin Prefecture to threaten Quanzhong. Xingxi killed every commissioner, seized their edicts, and sent them to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 又遣中使徵兵於王建，朱全忠亦遣使乞師於建。

translations.literal: Palace commissioners were also sent to summon troops from Wang Jian; Zhu Quanzhong also sent envoys requesting troops from Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Palace commissioners were also sent to summon Wang Jian's troops—and Quanzhong sent envoys requesting reinforcements from him as well.

sentences.zh: 建外修好於全忠，罪狀李茂貞，而陰勸茂貞堅守，許之救援。

translations.literal: Jian outwardly cultivated good relations with Quanzhong and denounced Li Maozhen, but secretly urged Maozhen to hold firm and promised him rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian openly courted Quanzhong and denounced Maozhen, but secretly urged Maozhen to hold out and promised to send help.

sentences.zh: 以武信節度使王宗佶、前東川節度使王宗滌等為扈駕指揮使，將兵五萬，聲言迎軍駕，其實襲茂貞山南諸州。

translations.literal: Wuxin military commissioner Wang Zongji, former Dongchuan military commissioner Wang Zongdi, and others were made escort commanders, leading fifty thousand troops, proclaiming they would welcome the imperial carriage but in fact striking Maozhen's southern mountain prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian named Wang Zongji of Wuxin and Wang Zongdi of Dongchuan escort commanders and sent fifty thousand men—claiming to welcome the emperor but actually raiding Maozhen's southern prefectures.

sentences.zh: 江西節度使鍾傳將兵圍撫州刺史危全諷，天火燒其城，士民歡驚。

translations.literal: Jiangxi military commissioner Zhong Chuan led troops to besiege Fu Prefecture governor Wei Quanfeng; heaven's fire burned his city, and officials and commoners cried out in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi commissioner Zhong Chuan besieged Fu Prefecture governor Wei Quanfeng when a fire from heaven broke out in the city, throwing officials and commoners into panic.

sentences.zh: 諸將請急攻之，傳曰：「乘人之危，非仁也。」

translations.literal: The generals asked to attack urgently; Chuan said: "Taking advantage of another's peril is not humane."
translations.idiomatic: His generals urged an immediate assault. Chuan said: "Striking a man when he is down is not humane."

sentences.zh: 乃祝曰：「全諷之罪，無為害民。」

translations.literal: He then prayed: "Let Quanfeng's guilt not harm the people."
translations.idiomatic: He prayed instead: "Let Quanfeng's guilt not harm the people."

sentences.zh: 火尋止。

translations.literal: The fire soon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The fire soon died out.

sentences.zh: 全諷聞之，謝罪聽命，以女妻傳子匡時。

translations.literal: Quanfeng heard of it, apologized and submitted to orders, and gave his daughter in marriage to Chuan's son Kuangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Quanfeng heard of this, submitted in apology, and gave his daughter to Chuan's son Kuangshi in marriage.

sentences.zh: 傳少時嘗獵，醉遇虎，與鬥，虎搏其肩，而傳亦持虎腰不置。

translations.literal: When Chuan was young he once went hunting; drunk he met a tiger and fought it—the tiger struck his shoulder, but Chuan also seized the tiger's waist and would not let go.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Chuan went hunting drunk, met a tiger, and fought it. The tiger clawed his shoulder, but Chuan grabbed its midsection and would not let go.

sentences.zh: 旁人共殺虎，乃得免。

translations.literal: Those nearby together killed the tiger, and only then was he spared.
translations.idiomatic: Others killed the tiger and saved him.

sentences.zh: 既貴，悔之，常戒諸子曰：「士處世貴智謀，勿效吾暴虎也。」

translations.literal: Once honored, he regretted it and often admonished his sons, saying: "A gentleman in the world values wisdom and strategy—do not imitate my fighting a tiger bare-handed."
translations.idiomatic: After he rose to power he regretted it and often warned his sons: "A gentleman succeeds by wit and strategy—do not imitate my bare-handed fight with a tiger."

sentences.zh: 武貞節度使雷滿薨，子彥威自稱留後。

translations.literal: Wuzhen military commissioner Lei Man died; his son Yanwei declared himself acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Man, military commissioner of Wuzhen, died; his son Yanwei declared himself acting commissioner.
